# Index of modules

The task guides, every registry kind, then every module of the engine and its tools: what it is for (its file
comment's first sentence), what it exports and the tests that cover it. Each export, with the first sentence of its
doc comment, is in [API.md](API.md); error and advice codes are in [ERRORS.md](ERRORS.md).

## Start here

The task guides, as AGENTS.md lists them under "Where things are", and the skills: read each when the task needs
it.

- [`docs/PROGRESS.md`](../docs/PROGRESS.md): read first, every session: where things stand, what is next, the open issues.
- [`docs/TESTING.md`](../docs/TESTING.md): the tiers, and which unit tests and specs a change selects.
- [`docs/PLAYGROUND.md`](../docs/PLAYGROUND.md): the playground (Phase 13): the site, the move set and its reference values, the five cameras, the two looks, and how feel and looks are checked.
- [`docs/HANDOFF.md`](../docs/HANDOFF.md): handing the engine to game agents (the prompt, many games at once), starting in a new environment, and the box against my-3d2dge's stress-world.
- [`lean/`](../lean/): the default handoff, the engine as a library (ADR-0024 amendment 1); docs/GAME-GUIDE.md and labs/game/, the full workspace's guide and starter. Keep lean/README.md, lean/game.html, the guide and the starter true when a public API changes (`x docs --write` rebuilds lean/my3dge.js and writes the generated blocks). tools/game/new-game.mjs makes a game; `node x engine --test` proves one passes its own gate.
- [`labs/box/README.md`](../labs/box/README.md): the box's scenes, settings and quick loop; adding a scene or a variant (a variant is a new scene file or a settings preset, never a change of meaning in a passing scene).
- [`tests/replays/README.md`](../tests/replays/README.md): the replay format; checking, recording and making replays.
- [`tools/templates/`](../tools/templates/): `node x new <kind> <id>` writes a module, scene, material… from its kind's template and checks it (`node x new` lists the kinds).
- [`.claude/skills/`](../.claude/skills/): the skills, each loaded when its description says (x-loop after any change, stress-box for the box, determinism-debugging when hashes part, rapier, three-webgpu, escalation).
  - [`.claude/skills/determinism-debugging/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/determinism-debugging/SKILL.md): How to find and fix a determinism bug in my-3dge. Use whenever x replay, a replay test or a hash comparison fails.
  - [`.claude/skills/escalation/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/escalation/SKILL.md): When and how to escalate to the owner in my-3dge. Use before any such action, and when the SessionStart hook or the Stop hook names an open escalation.
  - [`.claude/skills/rapier/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/rapier/SKILL.md): Rapier physics in my-3dge under the reproducibility contract. Use when adding bodies, colliders or queries, touching engine/physics, or debugging a physics hash or capture.
  - [`.claude/skills/stress-box/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/stress-box/SKILL.md): The Stress Box (labs/box), the engine's integration target. Use when you work on the box, add or tune a box scene, or need to show an engine capability in the box.
  - [`.claude/skills/three-webgpu/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/three-webgpu/SKILL.md): Writing three.js code in my-3dge. Use before writing, reviewing or debugging code that imports three.js.
  - [`.claude/skills/x-loop/SKILL.md`](../.claude/skills/x-loop/SKILL.md): The my-3dge work loop, edit → check → test → report. Use whenever you change code in this repository, or are unsure what to run next.

## Kinds

Every registry kind (PLAN.md §6.6), from its `defineKind` call: `node x describe <kind>` lists its fields and ids.

| Kind              | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Declared in                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `action`          | A multi-beat sequence played on a body: beats of body states, clips, IK targets, flips and events. The engine's set is data/anim/actions/, one file each (loadActions).                                                            | [`engine/anim/actions-data.ts`](../engine/anim/actions-data.ts)               |
| `actionMap`       | Named actions and the physical codes bound to each (keys by KeyboardEvent.code, mouse, pad by position): what the input devices turn into intents.                                                                                 | [`engine/input/actionMaps.ts`](../engine/input/actionMaps.ts)                 |
| `body`            | Puppet bodies: parts on the humanoid skeleton, one line each, with material slots (the palette).                                                                                                                                   | [`engine/gfx/puppets/grammar.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/grammar.ts)           |
| `build`           | Body proportions for the humanoid skeleton, in metres before size (limbs, torso, head, stance, gait).                                                                                                                              | [`engine/anim/builds.ts`](../engine/anim/builds.ts)                           |
| `camera`          | A game's own camera mode: its code cam3=<name>[,…] and the function that makes it (engine/gfx/cameras/define.ts).                                                                                                                  | [`engine/gfx/cameras/define.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/define.ts)             |
| `clipset`         | A set of readable clips loaded for playing (PLAN.md §10): its header and its clips. The library is data/anim/sets/, one directory a set, which a page or tool reads and registers (defineClipSet).                                 | [`engine/anim/clip/clipsets.ts`](../engine/anim/clip/clipsets.ts)             |
| `component`       | Component kinds: the plain-object data entities hold (e.position), with their fields. The canonical state and the hash read every component's declared fields, in order.                                                           | [`engine/sim/state.ts`](../engine/sim/state.ts)                               |
| `course`          | A feel course: a scripted run of a scene (a replay’s inputs) and the numbers to measure on it, each against its reference and tolerance (node x feel).                                                                             | [`engine/dev/feel/course.ts`](../engine/dev/feel/course.ts)                   |
| `devAction`       | Dev actions: changes made to a running scene between steps (god mode, freeze, spawn, travel, time scale), recorded in replays.                                                                                                     | [`engine/sim/devActions.ts`](../engine/sim/devActions.ts)                     |
| `emitter`         | Emitters: particle effects as data (how particles start, move and look), burst where something happens, answering event types, or running at a rate with a flickering light.                                                       | [`engine/gfx/fx/emitters.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/emitters.ts)                   |
| `feature`         | Optional GPU features and techniques: what each needs, what is lost without it, and its advice code.                                                                                                                               | [`engine/gfx/features.ts`](../engine/gfx/features.ts)                         |
| `geometry`        | Shapes props, levels and bodies name by id: a builder of a three.js BufferGeometry with its parameters and a vertex budget.                                                                                                        | [`engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.ts)       |
| `glyph`           | Level legend glyphs: what one map character means (heights, floor shape, solid, collider and mesh recipes, nav flags, spawn, light spot, surface, footprint; in a storey, void, full height, openings, heads and room markers).    | [`engine/world/level/glyph.ts`](../engine/world/level/glyph.ts)               |
| `inspectorMember` | Members of the inspector (__engine, createHeadless): a call or property with its help line, argument schema and implementation.                                                                                                    | [`engine/dev/members.ts`](../engine/dev/members.ts)                           |
| `level`           | Levels: a level text (front matter and a map in legend characters) that compileLevel turns into data.                                                                                                                              | [`engine/world/level/level.ts`](../engine/world/level/level.ts)               |
| `light`           | What a level's light spot shines with: three.js's PointLight parameters, its priority in the light pool and its flicker.                                                                                                           | [`engine/gfx/lights.ts`](../engine/gfx/lights.ts)                             |
| `look`            | Looks: a material style plus a filter chain (post-processing), and the sky that lights it, as whole looks or one-filter presets.                                                                                                   | [`engine/gfx/post/looks.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/looks.ts)                     |
| `material`        | Materials as data with three.js's classic parameters (color, map, roughness, emissive, flags); the engine decides how to draw them.                                                                                                | [`engine/gfx/materials/material.ts`](../engine/gfx/materials/material.ts)     |
| `move`            | A named strike: the swing (arc, height, reach, plane), what strikes, the body motion, the phase times and the hit window.                                                                                                          | [`engine/anim/moves-data.ts`](../engine/anim/moves-data.ts)                   |
| `movement`        | How a character moves: the controller’s settings it sets and, for the shooter model, its numbers (speeds, accelerations, air control, the jump’s fatigue, the lurch, the fall stun). Taken with createCharacter({ movement: id }). | [`engine/physics/movement/profile.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/profile.ts) |
| `prop`            | Props: things that stand in a level, as data: meshes (geometry and material by id), a body, an optional light spot, where a level places them, and interaction hooks.                                                              | [`engine/world/props/prop.ts`](../engine/world/props/prop.ts)                 |
| `scene`           | Scenes: a level, settings, a setup and a step, sim-side, so x sim, x replay and createHeadless run them in Node.                                                                                                                   | [`engine/sim/scene.ts`](../engine/sim/scene.ts)                               |
| `setting`         | The engine's and the game's settings, by dotted path: one schema for x set, URL parameters and __engine.set.                                                                                                                       | [`engine/core/settings.ts`](../engine/core/settings.ts)                       |
| `sfx`             | A sound effect: voices for the DSP core, layers of other effects, variants and a mixer bus.                                                                                                                                        | [`engine/audio/data/sfx.ts`](../engine/audio/data/sfx.ts)                     |
| `site`            | Sites: levels standing on a terrain, each placed at an offset and a quarter turn.                                                                                                                                                  | [`engine/world/site.ts`](../engine/world/site.ts)                             |
| `sky`             | Sky presets: what surrounds and lights a level (background, dome, backdrop, sun, ambient light, fog, how bright the point lights shine).                                                                                           | [`engine/gfx/sky.ts`](../engine/gfx/sky.ts)                                   |
| `song`            | A looping tune in tracker notation: tempo, bars and tracks of notes or drum tokens.                                                                                                                                                | [`engine/audio/data/song.ts`](../engine/audio/data/song.ts)                   |
| `strikable`       | How an entity holding a component takes a strike (doors, breakables, WP 13.16).                                                                                                                                                    | [`engine/sim/interact.ts`](../engine/sim/interact.ts)                         |
| `telegraph`       | Telegraphs: an attack's warning shape on the floor (arc, ring, line or cone, in metres), drawn as it winds up and tested for hits and near misses when it goes off.                                                                | [`engine/world/telegraphs.ts`](../engine/world/telegraphs.ts)                 |
| `terrain`         | Terrain: outdoor ground as a seeded heightfield (noise, hills, terraces, flattened footprints).                                                                                                                                    | [`engine/world/terrain.ts`](../engine/world/terrain.ts)                       |
| `texture`         | Seeded, periodic texture generators: colour, height, roughness and emissive per texel, with their parameters, size, tile, density and look.                                                                                        | [`engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts)         |
| `thing`           | Things that can be hit: a range’s targets, a ring’s dummies; they count hits, go down and come back up, and slide along a track.                                                                                                   | [`engine/world/things.ts`](../engine/world/things.ts)                         |
| `touchlayout`     | A page's touch controls: the buttons in the corner fan, each pressing an action, and whether the menu button shows.                                                                                                                | [`engine/ui/touch.ts`](../engine/ui/touch.ts)                                 |
| `usable`          | How an entity holding a component is used (doors, switches): its prompt and its use (WP 13.16).                                                                                                                                    | [`engine/sim/interact.ts`](../engine/sim/interact.ts)                         |
| `weapon`          | Firearms: fire rate, damage, range, spread, recoil, magazine, reloads, sights, draw time, muzzle and look.                                                                                                                         | [`engine/world/weapons.ts`](../engine/world/weapons.ts)                       |

## The root

- [`eslint.config.js`](../eslint.config.js): ESLint's settings for T0 (PLAN.md §6.10; `npm run lint`, inside `npm run check`): typescript-eslint's recommended rules without type information (so T0 stays fast), the file-comment and size rules, then the doctrine's rule families from tools/eslint/, one block per family, each message naming the fix.
  - Exports: `configure`, `default`, `SWITCHES`
- [`playwright.config.ts`](../playwright.config.ts): Playwright Test's settings for T2 (PLAN.md §6.10, §8.8): one project, `webgpu`, on the platform's Chromium with shardfall's WebGPU flags, against a Vite dev server it starts itself.
  - Exports: `default`
- [`vite.config.ts`](../vite.config.ts): Vite's settings (the dev server and the build) and Vitest's (T1), in one file as Vitest expects (PLAN.md §6.10, WPs 0.2 and 0.12).
  - Exports: `default`
  - Tests: [`tools/lib/vite.test.ts`](../tools/lib/vite.test.ts)

## engine/anim/locomotion

- [`locks.ts`](../engine/anim/locomotion/locks.ts): The foot plant's stance locks (PLAN.md WP 13.10, the rule ADR-0009 amendment 8 asked for; ADR-0025 amendment 10): `holdFoot` keeps a sole where it landed while its body says the foot stands (the humanoid's `stance()`: the planted stride's contact window, engine/anim/locomotion/planted.ts), and lets it go over `FOOT_LOCK.release` once the window ends, lifting as its animation lifts it, so a push-off never drags it along the floor (at once when its animation took it up, but a toe-off in its stride on the level it held on: it eases out of a lock the body sped away from).

  - Exports: `MATRIX_MOVE`, `MOVEMENT_STATES`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/locomotion/matrix.test.ts`](../engine/anim/locomotion/matrix.test.ts)
- [`motion.ts`](../engine/anim/locomotion/motion.ts): What the playground's movement tells the view's animation (PLAN.md WP 13.10, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.1): the shooter model's state (the component `motion`, engine/physics/movement/model.ts: its mode, duck, slide, floor and landing) and the actor's velocity, read on the view's side as plain data, so the animation follows the movement without the sim's animator holding more than it does (its state is hashed; this is presentation, and no replay golden changes).
  - Exports: `BodyView`, `MotionView`, `MOVEMENT_POSE`, `MovementPose`, `plantsFeet`

- [`planted.ts`](../engine/anim/locomotion/planted.ts): The planted stride (PLAN.md WP 13.10, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.1; ADR-0025 amendment 10): how a build with `plantedStride` (the playground's adult) steps so a foot on the ground stays where it landed.
  - Exports: `footCycle`, `PLANTED`, `plantedBob`, `plantedDuty`, `plantedEase`, `plantedHeight`, `plantedKnee`, `plantedMove`, `plantedStep`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/locomotion/planted.test.ts`](../engine/anim/locomotion/planted.test.ts)
- [`shown.ts`](../engine/anim/locomotion/shown.ts): The view's movement poses (PLAN.md WP 13.10, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.1): what the body shows of its movement beyond the sim's state (`ShownMovement`, `Humanoid.shown`, eased by engine/anim/locomotion/motion.ts `MovementPose`), as effector layers the pose tables take in (engine/anim/poses.ts: `SHOWN_FOOT_LAYERS` after the crouch, `SHOWN_HAND_LAYERS` after the air) and as the pelvis's and the spine's share (`SHOWN`, read by engine/anim/locomotion.ts): - the slide: the right leg out ahead, the left folded under, both soles a few centimetres off the floor; the left hand trailing behind, its fingertips just over the ground, the right forward for balance; the pelvis low and leaned back, the spine tilted toward the slope it slides on (`pitch`); - the air by the vertical speed: rising, the legs tuck tighter; falling, they reach down for the ground and the arms rise out for balance (the apex between: the humanoid's own tuck); - the landing's dip (`land`): the pelvis drops, a soft one a little, a hard one (`hard`) deep, leaning forward with the right hand down on the floor ahead (a three-point landing); - the lean into the acceleration and the bank into a turn (`lean`, `bank`: the spine).
  - Exports: `createShown`, `SHOWN`, `SHOWN_FOOT_LAYERS`, `SHOWN_HAND_LAYERS`, `ShownMovement`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/locomotion/shown.test.ts`](../engine/anim/locomotion/shown.test.ts)

## engine/anim/traversal

- [`clear.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/clear.ts): Keeping a traversing body's legs out of the wall it traverses (PLAN.md WP 13.11, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.1), for the traversal plant (engine/anim/traversal/plant.ts) after each leg's solve: - the wall (`faceOf`): a mantle's face under its lip, a low ledge's too (a point on it, its normal out toward the body, the lip's height as its top), or a climb's wall, a skin off the hull's front where it last climbed (`TraversalPose.wallAt`, kept while the body is near it and takes no other way, `walled`); a wall reaches `CLEAR.deep` past its face, so a fence's far side, open ground, is never in it; - a solved leg kept off it (`clearLeg`): its toes' tip moved out with the foot, then its knee kept `CLEAR.knee` off it until the kneecap clears the top, swung out to its side (and up over the lip once the hip is over it), each no further than that takes (so the swing grows smoothly as a foot steps up the face), and a leg that clears it is left exactly as it was; - a solved arm kept off it (`clearArm`): its elbow `CLEAR.elbow` off it, swung down, out and back; and a hand on its way to a contact kept in front of the face until it rises over the top (`keepOff`), so a reach for a lip goes up the face, never through it.
  - Exports: `CLEAR`, `clearArm`, `clearLeg`, `Face`, `faceOf`, `inside`, `keepOff`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/traversal/plant.test.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/plant.test.ts)
- [`contacts.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/contacts.ts): Where a traversing body's hands and feet touch (PLAN.md WP 13.11, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.1): the contacts the view's traversal poses put them on (engine/anim/traversal/pose.ts), from the shooter model's state as plain data (`TraversalView`, the component `motion`: engine/physics/movement/model.ts), the ride it is on (`RideView`, the component `zipline` or `ladder`: engine/world/traverse.ts) and its hull (`HullView`), all read on the view's side.
  - Exports: `cableGrips`, `climbCycle`, `climbHoldHeight`, `hullOf`, `HullView`, `ladderLimb`, `Limb`, `lowPull`, `mantleGrips`, `mantleHold`, `mantleShare`, `rideOf`, `RideView`, `TRAVERSAL`, `TraversalView`, `wallPoint`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/traversal/contacts.test.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/contacts.test.ts)
- [`hold.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/hold.ts): Holding and aiming (PLAN.md WP 13.11, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.1): the layer that ends the animator's `post` slot, after the traversal plant (engine/anim/traversal/plant.ts), posing what the body does with its look and its weapon from what the view tells it before each pose: - the head and eyes toward the aim (`look`: the heading and pitch the player looks along, from the page's intents; ADR-0025 amendment 10 sent them here), the neck and the head sharing the turn within their limits (engine/anim/ik.ts `aim`, its chain without the chest, so the hands on what they hold stay there); - a gun carried (`carry`, as the view says, else the body's weapon `gun`): its stock at the right shoulder, the right hand on its grip and the left on its handguard (two-hand IK, `handTo`), held low and ready (`HOLD.ready` below the aim), raised along the aim when aiming down the sights (`aiming`: its sight line through the right eye, `HOLD.sights`), lowered and turned across the body at a sprint, the hands low (the gait's speed past the run, `HOLD.sprint`); its barrel follows the aim's pitch and, within `HOLD.yaw` of the body's heading, its yaw, the chest turning with it (the aim offsets), the hand along the barrel so the muzzle points where the aim does, the left hand slid back along the handguard to stay in reach (`support`), the gun drawn in past that; - a traversal holding the hands (`busy`: `TraversalPose.weight`), or the traversal plant's hands on a contact (`contacts`: a hard landing's hand), lowers the hold as far as they hold them, and the head turns half as far.
  - Exports: `HeldLook`, `HOLD`, `HoldPlant`, `Look`, `LookPose`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/traversal/hold.test.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/hold.test.ts)
- [`matrix.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/matrix.ts): The traversal and holding states of the state matrix (PLAN.md WP 13.11, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.1): the ways the playground's player traverses and holds, as `stateMatrix` runs them (engine/anim/stateMatrix.ts), so the anim QA family measures them and `x sheet` draws them for a `plantedStride` build (tools/qa/anim.ts `humanoidStates`, ids `traversal:<name>` and `hold:<name>`): the 2 m mantle (`grab`), the grab held as a hang (`hang`), a 1 m wall vaulted at a sprint (`vault`), a wall-climb let go (`climb`), up and back down a ladder (`ladder`), a zipline ridden and let go (`zipline`), the skydive's glide, dive and landing (`skydive`), a slide-jump (`slideJump`), a gun aimed through a sweep of pitch and heading (`hold:aim`) and lowered at a sprint (`hold:sprint`).
  - Exports: `TRAVERSAL_STATES`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/traversal/matrix.test.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/matrix.test.ts)
- [`plant.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/plant.ts): The traversal plant (PLAN.md WP 13.11, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.1): the layer that poses a traversing body at the end of the animator's `post` slot, after the foot plant (engine/anim/footPlant.ts), from the view's `TraversalPose` (engine/anim/traversal/pose.ts), which the view sets on it before each pose (`pose`): - the body: a skydive tilted onto its front (spread in its glide, its arms back in its dive), upright again in its landing pose; drawn `TRAVERSAL_PLANT.ladder` nearer a ladder than its hull stands; and moved toward the hands as far as they need to reach what they hold (a mantle's press up past the lip, a high grab, a short build's cable); - the free limbs: a mantle's legs hanging under the lip, the grab's right foot stepping up the face late in it and the pull's left after it, each onto the top as the hip rises past the lip; a low ledge's legs tucked (swung aside in a vault); a zipline's legs swinging with the ride; the skydive's spread, dive and landing; a slide-jump's legs out ahead, reaching down as it falls, its arms forward and up; - the limbs on contacts (`TraversalPose.targets`): each hand's grip socket and each foot's contact socket solved onto its target as far as its weight says (the knees forward, the elbows down and out under a hand over the shoulder, back behind one under it), the wrist in line with the forearm, flat on a top, a foot level on a hold or a rung; each leg kept out of the wall it traverses (engine/anim/traversal/clear.ts); and a hard landing's right hand (the humanoid's shown `land`, WP 13.10) put down flat on the floor at the bottom of its dip.
  - Exports: `swingGrip`, `TRAVERSAL_PLANT`, `TraversalPlant`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/traversal/plant.test.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/plant.test.ts)
- [`pose.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/pose.ts): The view's traversal poses (PLAN.md WP 13.11, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.1): `TraversalPose` follows what the shooter model's state says the body does (`TraversalView`, engine/anim/traversal/contacts.ts) once a sim step and eases a weight for each way it traverses (`TRAVERSALS`): a mantle (the grab, the hang, the pull, a low ledge vaulted at a run with one hand), a wall-climb, a ladder, a zipline, a skydive (its spread glide, its dive, its landing pose) and a slide-jump.
  - Exports: `createLimbTargets`, `layTarget`, `LimbTarget`, `Traversal`, `TRAVERSAL_POSE`, `TraversalPose`, `TRAVERSALS`
  - Tests: [`engine/anim/traversal/pose.test.ts`](../engine/anim/traversal/pose.test.ts)

- [`look.ts`](../engine/app/look.ts): The page's look (PLAN.md WP 7.8, §6.7, ADR-0008 amendment 10): what `createEngine` (engine/app/engine.ts) does before every warm-up, frame and shot, so the look the view setting `post.look` names (engine/gfx/post/looks.ts) reaches the whole picture and not only the post chain's filters (engine/gfx/post/chain.ts): - **its sky:** the stage's lights show the look's sky, or the stage's own for `''` (engine/gfx/stageSky.ts), with the quality tier's shadow budget (engine/gfx/quality.ts), its dome as the look's gradient asks (`skyGradient`); - **its shells:** the outline shells round the stage's props and bodies, as the look's `shells` ask (WP 13.24, engine/gfx/stageShells.ts); - **its material style:** the page's style set (engine/gfx/materials/styles.ts), which the chain switches, joins the warm-up the first time a look asks for a style other than the set's own, so every warm-up from then on compiles the drawn meshes in the set's own style and in each style a look has asked for; and while it is joined, meshes shown since the last frame (a crowd entering, a stand-in) are re-pointed to the style drawn now.

## engine/audio/dsp

- [`biquad.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/biquad.ts): Biquad filters of the DSP core (PLAN.md WP 9.1): the eight types of Web Audio's `BiquadFilterNode` (lowpass, highpass, bandpass, notch, allpass, peaking, lowshelf, highshelf), with the coefficients of Robert Bristow-Johnson's Audio EQ Cookbook, which Web Audio's own formulas come from.
  - Exports: `Biquad`, `FILTER_TYPES`, `FilterType`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/biquad.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/biquad.test.ts)
- [`delay.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/delay.ts): The delay (echo) effect of the DSP core (PLAN.md WP 9.1): a feedback delay line, as a `DelayNode` looped through a feedback `GainNode` and mixed back with the dry signal is in Web Audio.
  - Exports: `echo`, `ECHO_FLOOR`, `echoCount`, `echoSpacing`, `EchoSpec`, `MAX_ECHOES`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/delay.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/delay.test.ts)
- [`envelope.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/envelope.ts): Volume envelopes of the DSP core (PLAN.md WP 9.1): the source's percussive envelope (a linear attack, then an exponential fall to 0.0005 at the end, as Web Audio's `exponentialRampToValueAtTime` gives it) and ADSR (attack, decay, sustain, release), which also covers the source's `hold` (sustain at full volume, a 30 ms release).
  - Exports: `AdsrEnvelope`, `Envelope`, `envelopeCurve`, `FALL_FLOOR`, `FallEnvelope`, `holdEnvelope`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/envelope.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/envelope.test.ts)
- [`measure.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/measure.ts): Numbers about rendered samples (PLAN.md WP 9.1, §8.5; doctrine: Verifiable without a display): peak, RMS, DC offset and the amplitude of one frequency (Goertzel's algorithm), so tests and tools judge a sound by numbers instead of by ear.
  - Exports: `dcOffset`, `peak`, `rms`, `toneAmplitude`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/measure.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/measure.test.ts)
- [`osc.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/osc.ts): The tonal oscillators of the DSP core (PLAN.md WP 9.1; doctrine: Quality under the hood): square, pulse 25%, pulse 12.5%, triangle, sine and saw, each a function of a phase.
  - Exports: `blamp`, `blep`, `DUTY`, `oscillate`, `TONAL_WAVES`, `TonalWave`, `wrap`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/osc.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/osc.test.ts)
- [`pluck.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/pluck.ts): The Karplus–Strong pluck of the DSP core (PLAN.md WP 9.1): a burst of seeded noise circulating in a delay line whose loop averages neighbouring samples, so it rings like a plucked string and darkens as it decays.
  - Exports: `Pluck`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/pluck.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/pluck.test.ts)
- [`render.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/render.ts): The DSP core's entry point (PLAN.md WP 9.1, §6.5, ADR-0013; doctrines: Assets, Reproducible, Verifiable): `render(def, seed, rate)` turns a sound definition (engine/audio/dsp/voice.ts) into a `Float32Array` of mono samples, and `soundHash` digests one, so every sound is code, renders in Node, and checks by its hash.
  - Exports: `DEFAULT_RATE`, `render`, `RENDER_CODES`, `soundHash`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts), [`tests/e2e/audio-dsp.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/audio-dsp.spec.ts)
- [`synth.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/synth.ts): One voice rendered into samples (PLAN.md WP 9.1): the pitch path (an exponential sweep, the arpeggio's steps, vibrato), the source (a tonal oscillator with optional FM, seeded white noise, or a Karplus–Strong pluck), the filter, the envelope and the echo, in that order, added into the sound's buffer at the voice's start.
  - Exports: `renderVoice`, `voiceEnd`, `voiceSamples`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts)
- [`voice.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/voice.ts): A sound definition and its checks (PLAN.md WP 9.1; doctrines: Assets, Agent-operable): a sound is plain data, one voice or a list of voices played together, in the source chip synth's words (`wave`, `freq`, `to`, `dur`, `vol`, `attack`, `hold`, `arp`, `step`, `loop`, `vib`, `filter`, `q`), so its effects, drums and songs copy over as they are (WP 9.2), plus ADSR (`decay`, `sustain`, `release`), a start time `at`, an explicit filter, `fm`, `pluck` and a `delay` echo.
  - Exports: `DelaySpec`, `FilterSpec`, `FmSpec`, `MAX_SECONDS`, `normalizeSound`, `NormalVoice`, `noteFreq`, `Pitch`, `PluckSpec`, `SoundDef`, `Voice`, `VOICE_CODES`, `Wave`, `WAVES`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/render.test.ts)

## engine/audio/runtime

- [`audio.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/audio.ts): The audio runtime (PLAN.md WP 9.3, §6.4, I-23; doctrines: Assets, Common ground): a page's sound.
  - Exports: `Audio`, `AUDIO_CODES`, `AudioInfo`, `AudioOptions`, `AudioState`, `createAudio`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/runtime/audio.test.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/audio.test.ts), [`tests/e2e/audio.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/audio.spec.ts)
- [`buffers.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/buffers.ts): Samples for Web Audio (PLAN.md WP 9.3): an effect or a song rendered by the DSP (engine/audio/data) becomes an `AudioBuffer`, and a song splits into its intensity layers, each laid out to loop without a seam.
  - Exports: `foldLoop`, `loopLayout`, `passSamples`, `renderLayers`, `SongLayer`, `songLayers`, `toBuffer`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/runtime/buffers.test.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/buffers.test.ts)
- [`gesture.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/gesture.ts): The user gestures that let a page make sound (PLAN.md WP 9.3; doctrine: Common ground): a browser starts an `AudioContext` only once the person at the page has acted, so the runtime (engine/audio/runtime/audio.ts) makes and resumes its context from inside one of these events, never before.
  - Exports: `GESTURE_EVENTS`, `GestureEvent`, `GestureTarget`, `isGesture`, `onGesture`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/runtime/gesture.test.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/gesture.test.ts)
- [`mixer.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/mixer.ts): The mixer (PLAN.md WP 9.3, I-23): four buses, `effects`, `music`, `ui` and `ambience`, into a master gain, with ducking and the room's reverb, as a Web Audio graph on any `BaseAudioContext` (a page's `AudioContext`, or an `OfflineAudioContext` in a test).
  - Exports: `AudioBus`, `BUS_VOLUMES`, `BUSES`, `createMixer`, `DUCK`, `Mixer`, `MixerInfo`, `ROOM_FADE`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/audio.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/audio.spec.ts)
- [`music.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/music.ts): The music player (PLAN.md WP 9.3, I-23): a `song` (engine/audio/data/song.ts) plays as its intensity layers (engine/audio/runtime/buffers.ts), looped in step on the `music` bus.
  - Exports: `createMusic`, `LAYER_FADE`, `Music`, `MUSIC_LEAD`, `MusicChange`, `MusicOptions`, `MusicPosition`, `nextLine`, `Quantize`, `SECTION_FADE`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/audio.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/audio.spec.ts)
- [`reverb.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/reverb.ts): Rooms and their reverb (PLAN.md WP 9.3, I-23; doctrine: Assets): each room preset is a few numbers, and its stereo impulse response is made from them as code, for Web Audio's `ConvolverNode`: no recorded impulse files.
  - Exports: `ABSORPTION`, `CONTENTS`, `impulseResponse`, `REVERB_CODES`, `roomAcoustics`, `RoomMake`, `RoomName`, `roomReverb`, `ROOMS`, `roomSpec`, `RoomSpec`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/runtime/reverb.test.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/reverb.test.ts)
- [`sound.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/sound.ts): One sound playing (PLAN.md WP 9.3): a rendered effect's `AudioBuffer` through its own gain, then, when it has a position, a lowpass for occlusion and a `PannerNode` (engine/audio/runtime/spatial.ts), into a mixer bus.
  - Exports: `checkPlay`, `createVoice`, `PlayOptions`, `RuntimeSound`, `Sound`, `SOUND_CODES`, `STOP_FADE`, `VoiceSpec`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/audio.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/audio.spec.ts)
- [`spatial.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/spatial.ts): Sound in 3D (PLAN.md WP 9.3, §6.1; doctrine: Common ground): Web Audio's `PannerNode` places a sound, its `AudioListener` follows the camera, and occlusion muffles a sound a wall stands in front of, asked of the sim's read-only `QueryView` (presentation only: nothing here changes play).
  - Exports: `listenerAxes`, `ListenerPose`, `muffling`, `occluded`, `OCCLUSION`, `PANNER`, `placeListener`, `placePanner`, `Vec3`, `wallsBetween`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/runtime/spatial.test.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/spatial.test.ts)
- [`voices.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/voices.ts): Voice limits (PLAN.md WP 9.3, I-23): how many sounds play at once, so a burst of hits never piles up into noise or clipping.
  - Exports: `createVoicePool`, `PooledVoice`, `VOICE_LIMITS`, `VoiceLimits`, `VoicePool`
  - Tests: [`engine/audio/runtime/voices.test.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/voices.test.ts)

## engine/core/fdlibm

- [`cbrt.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/cbrt.ts): The cube root in pure JavaScript, as V8 13.6 computes it (PLAN.md §6.5, WP U-8): a port of src/base/ieee754.cc's cbrt, FreeBSD's msun s_cbrt.c after Sun's fdlibm, so it gives Node 24's native bits.
  - Exports: `cbrt`
- [`exp.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/exp.ts): `exp` and `expm1` in pure JavaScript, as V8 13.6 computes them (PLAN.md §6.5, WP U-8): ports of src/base/ieee754.cc, which carries FreeBSD's msun after Sun's fdlibm, so they give Node 24's native bits.
  - Exports: `exp`, `expm1`
- [`hyperbolic.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/hyperbolic.ts): The hyperbolic functions and their inverses in pure JavaScript, as V8 13.6 computes them (PLAN.md §6.5, WP U-8): `sinh`, `cosh`, `tanh`, `asinh`, `acosh` and `atanh`, ports of src/base/ieee754.cc, which carries Sun's fdlibm through FreeBSD's msun, built on this folder's `exp`, `expm1`, `log` and `log1p`, so they give Node 24's native bits.
  - Exports: `acosh`, `asinh`, `atanh`, `cosh`, `sinh`, `tanh`
- [`inverse.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/inverse.ts): `asin`, `acos`, `atan` and `atan2` in pure JavaScript, as V8 13.6 computes them (PLAN.md §6.5, WP U-8): ports of src/base/ieee754.cc, which carries Sun's fdlibm through FreeBSD's msun, so they give Node 24's native bits.
  - Exports: `acos`, `asin`, `atan`, `atan2`
- [`log.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/log.ts): `log`, `log1p`, `log2` and `log10` in pure JavaScript, as V8 13.6 computes them (PLAN.md §6.5, WP U-8): ports of src/base/ieee754.cc, which carries FreeBSD's msun after Sun's fdlibm (`log10` the older fdlibm algorithm, through `log`; `log2` FreeBSD's, through `kLog1p`), so they give Node 24's native bits.
  - Exports: `log`, `log10`, `log1p`, `log2`
- [`remPio2.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/remPio2.ts): x mod π/2, as V8 13.6 reduces a trigonometric argument (PLAN.md §6.5, WP U-8): ports of src/base/ieee754.cc's __ieee754_rem_pio2 and __kernel_rem_pio2, Sun's fdlibm 5.3.
  - Exports: `NPIO2_HW`, `remPio2`, `TWO_OVER_PI`
- [`tan.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/tan.ts): The tangent in pure JavaScript, as V8 13.6 computes it (PLAN.md §6.5, WP U-8): ports of src/base/ieee754.cc's tan and __kernel_tan, Sun's fdlibm 5.3 (the kernel of 2004), reducing through engine/core/fdlibm/remPio2.ts, so it gives Node 24's native bits.
  - Exports: `tan`
- [`words.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/words.ts): The two 32-bit words of a double, as fdlibm reads and writes them (PLAN.md §6.5, WP U-8): the high word holds the sign, the exponent and the top 20 bits of the fraction, the low word the other 32.
  - Exports: `fromWords`, `high`, `low`, `withHigh`, `withLow`

- [`terrainSplat.ts`](../engine/gfx/terrainSplat.ts): The terrain's splat (PLAN.md WP 10.5): `createTerrainSplat(terrain, layers)` gives `wrap(material)`, what a terrain chunk (engine/gfx/terrain.ts) draws with: a node material copy of `material` (engine/gfx/materials/ nodeCopy.ts), the ground layer's material in whatever style the style set points it at (engine/gfx/materials/ styles.ts calls `wrap` through the chunks' `userData.restyle`), its colour mixing three layers at every fragment: - the ground: the material's own colour and map; - the steep, where the ground rises `terrain.steep` metres a metre or more (read off the fragment's world normal), blending in over ±`BAND` of that grade; - the high, from `terrain.high` metres over the terrain's origin up (none at 0), blending in over a metre either way; each layer its material's colour times its map at the map's repeat (the chunks' UVs are world metres), the steep over the high over the ground, the edges between them wavering by fractal noise over the ground (tslNoise.ts) so no contour line shows, and the whole varied ±8% at the scale of 24 m, as a level's floor is.
  - Exports: `BAND`, `createTerrainSplat`, `TerrainSplat`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/terrain.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/terrain.test.ts)

  - Exports: `AO`, `AO_CODES`, `AO_FEATURE`, `createOcclusion`, `Occlusion`

## engine/gfx/fx

- [`decals.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/decals.ts): Floor decals (PLAN.md WP 6.4): flat shapes lying on the floor, drawn by one instanced batch of quads (engine/gfx/instancing.ts, `fx:decals`) whose material cuts each shape out of its quad by its signed distance, so every edge is crisp at any size and every decal shares one pipeline and one draw.
  - Exports: `createDecals`, `DECAL`, `decalMaterial`, `Decals`, `DecalsOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/fx/decals.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/decals.test.ts)
- [`effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/effects.ts): The effects of a view (PLAN.md WP 6.4, §6.4's view state; doctrine: WebGPU only): `createEffects()` draws particles, floor decals and telegraphs, socket trails, bolts and camera shake for a scene, all under one group (`root`), as presentation the sim never sees: the sim hash is the same with effects on or off.
  - Exports: `BOLT`, `createEffects`, `Effects`, `EffectsOptions`, `FX_BUDGET`, `FxStats`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/fx/effects.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/effects.test.ts), [`tests/e2e/fx.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/fx.spec.ts)
- [`emitters.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/emitters.ts): Emitters (PLAN.md WP 6.4, §5.8, §6.6): the registry kind `emitter`, particle effects as data.
  - Exports: `defineEmitter`, `Emitter`, `EMITTER_FIELDS`, `emitterKind`, `EmitterLayer`, `EmitterSpec`, `FxLight`, `getEmitter`, `lightLevel`, `PARTICLE_FIELDS`, `ParticleFields`, `particleSpec`, `ParticleSpec`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/fx/emitters.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/emitters.test.ts)
- [`particles.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/particles.ts): CPU particles (PLAN.md WP 6.4, §6.4's view state): `ParticlePool` holds up to `capacity` live particles in flat arrays, bursts them from an emitter's `ParticleSpec` (engine/gfx/fx/emitters.ts) with a visual random stream (`fxRng`: never the sim's), and moves them a rendered frame at a time.
  - Exports: `BurstOptions`, `BurstPlan`, `PARTICLE_FLOATS`, `PARTICLE_STRIDE`, `ParticleBounds`, `ParticlePool`, `ParticleRing`, `ParticleStats`, `ParticleView`, `planBurst`, `writeParticle`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/fx/particles.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/particles.test.ts)
- [`payload.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/payload.ts): What an event carries for its effects (PLAN.md WP 6.4): `FxEventPayload`, the keys engine/gfx/fx/effects.ts reads of a sim event's payload, and how they become a burst.
  - Exports: `eventOptions`, `eventPosition`, `FxEventPayload`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/fx/effects.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/effects.test.ts)
- [`presets.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/presets.ts): The engine's emitters (PLAN.md WP 6.4, §5.8), as plain `emitter` specs (engine/gfx/fx/emitters.ts declares the kind and registers these with it): - **Shardfall's 13 presets**, its tuned numbers as they are (it uses the engine's axes and units): smoke, steam, sparks, embers, fountain, snow, rain, fireflies, magic, dust, bubbles, confetti and fire, each with its rate.
  - Exports: `BUILT_IN_EMITTERS`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/fx/emitters.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/emitters.test.ts)
- [`ribbons.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/ribbons.ts): Socket trails (PLAN.md WP 6.4): ribbons between a part's base and tip over its last positions, a blade's sweep or a claw's, from an animator's trail (engine/anim/character.ts `TrailSample`: base, tip, weight), fading to nothing at the tail.
  - Exports: `createRibbons`, `Ribbons`, `RibbonsOptions`, `TRAIL_TINTS`, `TrailSampleLike`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/fx/ribbons.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/ribbons.test.ts)
- [`rings.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/rings.ts): Floor rings (PLAN.md WP 6.4): a burst's shockwave or a laid decal, a band on the floor growing out and fading over its life (eased out: fast, then slow), drawn each frame through the decals (engine/gfx/fx/decals.ts) as a whole circle.
  - Exports: `createRings`, `Rings`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/fx/effects.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/effects.test.ts)
- [`shake.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/shake.ts): Screen shake (PLAN.md WP 6.4, §6.4: camera only): `ScreenShake` keeps an amplitude in metres that hits and explosions add to (capped at `SHAKE.max`) and that dies away by `exp(−9 t)`; `apply(camera)` moves the camera along its own right and up by two sums of sines of the presentation time, and `restore(camera)` takes the move back, so the view places the camera, applies the shake, draws, and restores.
  - Exports: `ScreenShake`, `SHAKE`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/fx/shake.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/shake.test.ts)
- [`sprites.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/sprites.ts): Sprites (PLAN.md WP 6.4): the particles and glows drawn as camera-facing quads through one instanced batch (engine/gfx/instancing.ts, `fx:sprites`), one material, so every emitter shares one pipeline and a burst never builds one.
  - Exports: `createSprites`, `spriteMaterial`, `Sprites`, `SpritesOptions`, `STREAK`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/fx/sprites.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/sprites.test.ts)

## engine/gfx/geometry

- [`box.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/box.ts): Boxes (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `boxGeometry({ width, height, depth })`, three.js's `BoxGeometry` with two changes the level meshes and props need: it stands on the ground (its bottom at y 0, centred in X and Z), and its UVs are in metres, so a texture keeps its density (16 texels per metre for the v1 textures) on every face whatever the box's size, instead of being stretched over each face.
  - Exports: `boxGeometry`, `BoxOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`builtins.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/builtins.ts): The geometry kit's built-in entries (PLAN.md WP 2.4): one `geometry` entry per builder of engine/gfx/geometry/, its parameters the builder's options as schema fields with the builder's defaults, and a vertex budget a little above what the defaults build.
  - Exports: `BUILT_IN_GEOMETRY`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.test.ts)
- [`checks.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/checks.ts): The geometry kit's codes and argument checks (PLAN.md WP 2.4): a builder given sizes it cannot build (a size of 0, a limb shorter than the difference of its radii, a ring whose inner radius is not below its outer) throws `GFX_BAD_GEOMETRY`, naming the shape, the problem and what to pass, before it writes a vertex.
  - Exports: `assertSegments`, `assertSizes`, `badGeometry`, `GEOMETRY_CODES`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`frustum.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/frustum.ts): Frustums, prisms and cylinders (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `frustumGeometry({ radiusBottom, radiusTop, height, radialSegments, smooth })`, three.js's `CylinderGeometry` standing on the ground, with UVs in metres: an octagonal dais, a brazier's bowl, a barrel, a cone (`radiusTop` 0), a well.
  - Exports: `frustumGeometry`, `FrustumOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`geometry.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.ts): The geometry registry (PLAN.md WP 2.4, §6.6, I-29): the registry kind `geometry`, one entry per shape a prop, a level or a body names by id (§6.1: `world` names geometry by id, `gfx` builds it).
  - Exports: `buildGeometry`, `defineGeometry`, `GEOMETRY_FIELDS`, `GeometryEntry`, `geometryKind`, `GeometryRef`, `GeometrySpec`, `getGeometry`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.test.ts)
- [`groups.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/groups.ts): Draw groups and merging (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `sidesThenTops(geometry)` sorts a geometry's triangles into two draw groups, its sides (material 0) then its tops and bottoms (material 1), so a box, a pillar or a wall drawn with a face material and a top material costs two draw calls instead of one per face; `mergeGeometries` joins indexed geometries with the same attributes into one.
  - Exports: `mergeGeometries`, `sidesThenTops`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`inspect.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/inspect.ts): Geometry measured as numbers (PLAN.md WP 2.4, §8.6, I-29): `inspectGeometry(geometry)` counts what the `geo` QA family (tools/qa/geo.ts) and the kit's tests check, in Node: vertices and triangles, missing attributes (`position`, `normal`, `uv`), index entries out of range, NaN or infinite numbers, degenerate triangles (an area below 1e-10 m²: a sliver no pixel shows, which breaks normals and physics hulls), normals that are not of length 1 (within 1e-3), triangles wound against their own normals (a corner's normal pointing away from the side the winding faces: the face is culled where it should show, or lit from behind), and the bounds.
  - Exports: `DEGENERATE_AREA`, `GeometryReport`, `inspectGeometry`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`limb.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/limb.ts): Tapered limbs (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `limbGeometry({ length, radiusStart, radiusEnd })`, the smooth hull of two spheres, one of `radiusStart` at the origin (the joint) and one of `radiusEnd` at `length` up +Y (the next joint): an upper arm, a thigh, a finger, a tail segment.
  - Exports: `limbGeometry`, `LimbOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`pillar.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/pillar.ts): Pillar parts (PLAN.md WP 2.4): the prototype's pillar, a plinth, a shaft of dressed stone and a capital of two slabs, as sizes (`pillarParts`) and as one geometry (`pillarGeometry`: the parts' boxes merged, sides then tops, so a pillar is two draw calls however many stand).
  - Exports: `pillarGeometry`, `PillarOptions`, `PillarPart`, `pillarParts`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`ramp.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/ramp.ts): Ramps and wedges (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `rampGeometry({ width, depth, low, high })`, a block standing on the ground whose top slopes from `low` at its -Z end up to `high` at its +Z end, so walking forward (+Z, the way characters face) climbs it.
  - Exports: `rampGeometry`, `RampOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`ring.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/ring.ts): Rings (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `ringGeometry({ innerRadius, outerRadius, height, radialSegments })`, a ring lying on the ground around the Y axis.
  - Exports: `ringGeometry`, `RingOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`roundedBox.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/roundedBox.ts): Rounded boxes (PLAN.md WP 2.4): `roundedBoxGeometry({ width, height, depth, radius, segments })`, a box whose edges and corners are rounded with `radius`, as three.js's `RoundedBoxGeometry` addon draws one, standing on the ground like every shape of the kit (its bottom at y 0, centred in X and Z), with UVs in metres and smooth normals.
  - Exports: `roundedBoxGeometry`, `RoundedBoxOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)
- [`writer.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/writer.ts): The geometry writer (PLAN.md WP 2.4): the one place the kit's builders (engine/gfx/geometry/) turn vertices and triangles into a three.js `BufferGeometry` with `position`, `normal` and `uv` and an index.

  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/kit.test.ts)

- [`flights.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/flights.ts): Flights of stairs between storeys (PLAN.md WP 13.14; docs/PLAYGROUND.md §6.1): `flightGeometry(tile, ramps, ground)` draws each ramp a flight glyph makes (engine/world/level/storeys.ts: a storey's floor to the next one's) as a house's stairs: `risersOf(ramp)` steps rising about `RISER` metres each, so 3 m between floors climb in 17 steps of 0.176 m, the flight's run shared out as their treads.

- [`chain.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/chain.ts): Post-processing (PLAN.md WP 7.4, §6.7, I-46): `createPost` sets up, once, one `PostProcessing` chain (r182) that every frame draws through, and draws the look the view settings name.

- [`grid.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/grid.ts): The pixel grid a frame draws on (PLAN.md WP 7.4, WP 13.24; docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.2): what the post chain (engine/gfx/post/chain.ts) works out each frame from its filter chain and the drawing buffer's lines.

  - Exports: `PRESETS`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/post/looks.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/looks.test.ts)

  - Exports: `createShading`, `Shading`, `SHADING_CODES`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/post/shading.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/shading.test.ts), [`tests/e2e/enhanced.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/enhanced.spec.ts)

## engine/gfx/post/shaders

- [`common.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/shaders/common.ts): The composite's small WGSL helpers (PLAN.md WP 7.4): brightness, noise, what the MRT's flags say about a pixel, linear depth, the Bayer threshold and the fixed palettes, each a TSL `wgslFn` that later functions include.
  - Exports: `postAimed`, `postBase`, `postBayer`, `postFlags`, `postHash`, `postHex`, `postLuma`, `postNoise`, `postPalette`, `postPart`, `postViewDepth`, `wgsl`, `WgslFunction`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/post.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/post.spec.ts)
- [`edges.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/shaders/edges.ts): The composite's edge filters (PLAN.md WP 7.4), as WGSL through TSL's `wgslFn`: - `post_edge`, the outline: a pixel is on an edge where, within the line's width, the depth jumps by more than a share of the distance (more at grazing angles), the surface creases (neighbouring normals part) or another outline group begins; only the nearer side is marked, so a line is one width thick, and the background is never outlined from inside (`shardfall:crates/pav_render/src/shaders/post.wgsl:72-101`, one sample, view-space normals); - `post_cel`, the prototype's comic cel: brightness in flat bands keeping each colour's hue (the darkest band above black), colour pushed, and ink on the darker side of sharp brightness changes and round every character's and object's silhouette (`my-3d2dge:src/stress-world/45-filters.js:47-60`); - `post_art_rim`, pixel art's one-block rim: a block whose neighbour block is another pixel-art object in front of it turns dark (`post.wgsl:761-804`).
  - Exports: `postArtRim`, `postCel`, `postEdge`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/post.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/post.spec.ts)
- [`stylize.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/shaders/stylize.ts): The painterly and print styles of the composite (PLAN.md WP 7.4), as WGSL through TSL's `wgslFn`, carried from shardfall (`shardfall:crates/pav_render/src/shaders/post.wgsl:431-697`), which 12 of its 73 presets and 7 of its 21 looks use: - **oil paint**: a generalized Kuwahara filter (Papari et al., with Kyprianidis et al.'s polynomial sector weights): eight overlapping sectors round the pixel each average their colours, and the calmest gets the weight, so areas turn into flat strokes while edges stay sharp; with a scope, samples from other parts are skipped, so no paint bleeds across; then brush strokes (noise drawn out along the picture's edges, lit from the top left) and canvas; - **halftone**: cyan, magenta, yellow and black dot screens at their classic angles on cream paper, each dot growing with the ink at its centre; with no colour kept, black dots only (newsprint); - **ASCII**: character cells whose brightness picks one of 12 glyphs (5 × 7 bitmaps packed into integers); - **pencil**: hatching families that appear as the picture darkens, contours where brightness changes fast, lines that wobble and redraw six times a second, and paper tinted by the colour kept.
  - Exports: `postAscii`, `postBrush`, `postDots`, `postHalftone`, `postHatch`, `postPaint`, `postSketch`, `postStylize`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/post.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/post.spec.ts)

- [`actors.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/actors.ts): Actors on the stage (PLAN.md WP 3.10, §6.4's view; I-21): every actor with an animator (engine/sim/actors.ts: an entity with the components `actor` and `animator`) drawn as a puppet (engine/gfx/puppets/draw.ts) of the neutral humanoid (`ACTOR_BODY`) or the body its component `puppet` names (`body:mannequin`, WP 8.9), in its animator's build, posed every frame by its animator's presentation half (engine/anim/character.ts `pose`) at the frame's alpha; an actor with clips (`clips`, engine/sim/actorClips.ts) has its clip layer laid over the body, loaded from the same data (a `ClipLayerPool` of the view's own, engine/anim/clip/clipsets.ts).

- [`blobShadow.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/blobShadow.ts): Blob shadows (PLAN.md WP 3.8): a soft dark disc on the floor under each body, all of them in one instanced batch (engine/gfx/instancing.ts), so a crowd's shadows cost one draw call.

## engine/gfx/textures

- [`bake.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/bake.ts): The CPU bake (PLAN.md WP 2.3, §6.7, I-20): runs a texture generator (engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts) over every texel and returns its maps as plain typed arrays, named as three.js's material slots name them: `map` (the colour, sRGB RGBA bytes), `heightMap` and `roughnessMap` (floats 0–1), `emissiveMap` (sRGB RGBA bytes, or null when nothing glows) and `normalMap` (tangent-space RGBA bytes, from the height).
  - Exports: `bakeKey`, `BakeSource`, `bakeTexture`, `newTexel`, `normalsFromHeight`, `TextureBake`, `TextureRef`, `textureSampler`, `TextureSampler`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/bake.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/bake.test.ts)
- [`codes.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/codes.ts): The texture codes (PLAN.md WP 2.3): the errors a bake raises for a size its pattern cannot tile at or a palette with no colours, each naming its fix (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
  - Exports: `TEXTURE_CODES`
- [`contactShadow.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/contactShadow.ts): Contact shadows and the level floor bake (PLAN.md WP 7.3, I-20): `levelFloorTexture(level, options)` returns a texture generator for one compiled level's whole floor, baked once over every tile as the prototype baked the hall's: a base texture (flagstones by default), moss creeping in from the foot of the walls (engine/gfx/textures/generators/moss.ts), a rune circle on each dais, glowing in the emissive map (engine/gfx/textures/generators/runes.ts), and a contact shadow, the soft dark band where a wall meets the floor, baked into the colour.
  - Exports: `CONTACT_SHADOW_CODES`, `contactShadow`, `ContactShadowOptions`, `FloorMossOptions`, `FloorRuneOptions`, `LevelFloorOptions`, `levelFloorTexture`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/contactShadow.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/contactShadow.test.ts)
- [`dataTexture.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/dataTexture.ts): A bake as three.js textures (PLAN.md WP 2.3, §6.7): `toDataTextures` turns a CPU bake (engine/gfx/textures/bake.ts) into `DataTexture`s for a material's slots, `map`, `normalMap`, `roughnessMap` and `emissiveMap`, each with its full mip chain computed on the CPU (engine/gfx/textures/mips.ts), repeating, and filtered for the look: `pixel` magnifies with nearest (crisp texels) and minifies with nearest texels blended between levels (no shimmer at a distance), `smooth` filters linearly on both, with 4× anisotropy for floors seen at a grazing angle.
  - Exports: `DataTextureOptions`, `TextureMaps`, `toDataTextures`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/dataTexture.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/dataTexture.test.ts)
- [`mips.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/mips.ts): Mipmaps on the CPU (PLAN.md WP 2.3, I-20): the full chain of a baked map down to 1 × 1, each level an area-weighted box filter of the one above, computed in the right space for what the map holds.
  - Exports: `linearToSrgbByte`, `mipChain`, `mipCount`, `MipEncoding`, `MipLevel`, `SRGB_TO_LINEAR`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/mips.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/mips.test.ts)
- [`seams.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/seams.ts): Texture quality measures (PLAN.md WP 2.3, §8.6, I-20): what the `tex` QA family (tools/qa/tex.ts) and the unit tests check a bake against.
  - Exports: `measureSeam`, `mipProblems`, `periodMismatch`, `rangeProblems`, `RangeReport`, `SEAM_LIMIT`, `SeamReport`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/seams.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/seams.test.ts)
- [`texture.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts): The generator registry (PLAN.md WP 2.3, §6.6, §6.7, I-20): the registry kind `texture`, one entry per seeded, periodic generator (engine/gfx/textures/types.ts says what a generator is), with its parameters as schema fields, the size it bakes at, the tile its pattern repeats at, its density in texels per metre and its look.
  - Exports: `assertSize`, `defineTexture`, `getTexture`, `sizeProblem`, `TEXTURE_FIELDS`, `TextureEntry`, `textureKind`, `textureParams`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/texture.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/texture.test.ts)
- [`tile.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/tile.ts): Tiling helpers for texture generators (PLAN.md WP 2.3, I-20): what a generator uses so its texels are a periodic function of the integer texel position, and its texture tiles without a seam.
  - Exports: `BondCell`, `cellHash`, `palette`, `pickTone`, `runningBond`, `tileNoise`, `TileNoiseOptions`, `wrapIndex`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/tile.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/tile.test.ts)
- [`tslNoise.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/tslNoise.ts): TSL noise for large-scale variation (PLAN.md WP 7.3, I-20): value noise and its fractal sum as TSL nodes, evaluated per pixel on the GPU in world space, so a tiled texture (a 4 m flagstone repeat) can be broken up over tens of metres without a bigger bake: `variationNode(options)` is a factor around 1 to multiply a material's colour by, slowly varying across the ground (`positionWorld.xz`, metres).
  - Exports: `fractalNode`, `fractalNoise`, `latticeHash`, `noiseNode`, `valueNoise`, `variationAt`, `variationNode`, `VariationOptions`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/tslNoise.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/tslNoise.test.ts)
- [`types.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/types.ts): What a texture generator is (PLAN.md WP 2.3, §6.7, I-20): a seeded, periodic function that writes four values per texel, its colour (albedo), its height (relief, from which the bake derives the normal map), its roughness and its emissive colour, so one generator gives every map a material needs.
  - Exports: `Texel`, `TexelFn`, `TextureContext`, `TextureLook`, `textureSpec`, `TextureSpec`
- [`v1.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/v1.ts): The engine's v1 texture generators (PLAN.md WP 2.3): flagstone, brick courses, dressed stone, planks, barrel staves and checker, by id.
  - Exports: `V1_TEXTURES`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)
- [`v2.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/v2.ts): The engine's v2 texture generators (PLAN.md WP 7.3): runes, moss, metal, plaster, dirt, grass and water, by id.
  - Exports: `V2_TEXTURES`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts)
- [`v3.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/v3.ts): The engine's v3 texture generators (PLAN.md WP 13.17): the building materials a house, a yard and a street need: asphalt, carpet, concrete, glass, shingles, siding, tiles, wallpaper and wood, by id.
  - Exports: `V3_TEXTURES`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts)

## engine/gfx/textures/generators

- [`asphalt.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/asphalt.ts): The asphalt generator (`texture:asphalt`, PLAN.md WP 13.17): a road's dark grey binder speckled with lighter stone chips and darker pits, in soft lighter patches where traffic has worn it.
  - Exports: `ASPHALT`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts)
- [`brick.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/brick.ts): The brick generator (`texture:brick`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): brick courses in running bond, each brick its own tone, a mortar joint along each course's bottom and each brick's right, a lit top row on every brick, and dark specks.
  - Exports: `BRICK`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)
- [`carpet.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/carpet.ts): The carpet generator (`texture:carpet`, PLAN.md WP 13.17): a close pile in its colour, each tuft a shade lighter or darker, mottled in soft patches where it has worn or been brushed the other way.
  - Exports: `CARPET`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts)
- [`checker.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/checker.ts): The checker generator (`texture:checker`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): square tiles of two colours, alternating (castle floors, bonus rooms, and a test pattern that shows how a surface is mapped).
  - Exports: `CHECKER`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)
- [`concrete.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/concrete.ts): The concrete generator (`texture:concrete`, PLAN.md WP 13.17): a path's or a foundation's pale grey, mottled at two scales, with small dark pores where air was caught.
  - Exports: `CONCRETE`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts)
- [`dirt.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/dirt.ts): The dirt generator (`texture:dirt`, PLAN.md WP 7.3): bare ground in soft patches of three tones at two scales, with pebbles, small clusters of two or three texels lit along their top and shaded along their bottom.
  - Exports: `DIRT`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts)
- [`flagstone.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/flagstone.ts): The flagstone generator (`texture:flagstone`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): square stones in running-bond rows, each its own tone from the palette, with a one-texel joint along its left and top, a lit bevel inside the joint and a shaded one along its bottom and right (light from the top left, as pixel art paints it), specks of grit, and a crack across some stones.
  - Exports: `FLAGSTONE`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)
- [`glass.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/glass.ts): The glass generator (`texture:glass`, PLAN.md WP 13.17): a window's pane, pale and cool, with soft reflections in diagonal bands across it: a broad one and a narrow one each repeat, as a sky catches in glass.
  - Exports: `GLASS`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts)
- [`grass.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/grass.ts): The grass generator (`texture:grass`, PLAN.md WP 7.3): turf in blotches of light and dark grass at two scales, short blade marks running up (dark where the turf is dark, light where it is light), and clusters of flowers, two-texel spots in yellow or white gathered in a few meadows rather than spread evenly.
  - Exports: `GRASS`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts)
- [`metal.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/metal.ts): The metal generator (`texture:metal`, PLAN.md WP 7.3): riveted iron plates, each with a seam along its bottom and left, a lit bevel inside its top and left and a shaded one along its bottom and right, brushed streaks along x in three tones, rivets along its top and bottom (a lit texel over a shaded one), and rust spreading from the seams in patches.
  - Exports: `METAL`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts)
- [`moss.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/moss.ts): The moss generator (`texture:moss`, PLAN.md WP 7.3): flagstones (engine/gfx/textures/generators/flagstone.ts, every one of its parameters) overgrown with moss.
  - Exports: `MOSS`, `mossGrowth`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts)
- [`planks.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/planks.ts): The plank generator (`texture:planks`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): floor boards running along x, a dark gap along the bottom of each board and at each board's end (the ends staggered per row), each board its own tone, and grain: streaks long along the board and short across it.
  - Exports: `PLANKS`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)
- [`plaster.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/plaster.ts): The plaster generator (`texture:plaster`, PLAN.md WP 7.3): a rendered wall, pale plaster mottled in three tones with fine grit and hairline cracks, and patches where it has fallen away to show brick courses beneath, each patch with a shaded rim where the plaster breaks off.
  - Exports: `PLASTER`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts)
- [`runes.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/runes.ts): The rune generator (`texture:runes`, PLAN.md WP 7.3): flagstones (engine/gfx/textures/generators/ flagstone.ts, every one of its parameters, in the hall's dusky palette) with a rune circle inlaid at the middle of each `cell`: an outer and an inner ring, spokes between them, a rune in each sector between the spokes, and a bright disc at the centre.
  - Exports: `paintRune`, `runeCircle`, `RuneCircleOptions`, `RuneMark`, `RUNES`, `RuneTones`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts)
- [`shingles.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/shingles.ts): The shingle generator (`texture:shingles`, PLAN.md WP 13.17): a roof's shingles in overlapping courses up the slope (v), each course offset half a shingle: a tone per shingle, a dark slot between shingles, a lit butt along each course's bottom row, and the shadow the course above throws across its top, so each dark row sits under the next course's light lip and reads as an overlap, not as mortar.
  - Exports: `SHINGLES`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts)
- [`siding.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/siding.ts): The siding generator (`texture:siding`, PLAN.md WP 13.17): painted clapboard, horizontal boards lapped down the wall (v up): a tone per board, its butt along the bottom catching the light, and the shadow the board above throws across its top row.
  - Exports: `SIDING`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts)
- [`staves.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/staves.ts): The barrel-stave generator (`texture:staves`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): staves running up, each its own tone and a dark gap along its right edge, the odd knot, and iron hoops across them (a lit top row, a shaded one under it), for a barrel's side wrapped round a cylinder (x round, y up).
  - Exports: `STAVES`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)
- [`stone.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/stone.ts): The dressed-stone generator (`texture:stone`, PLAN.md WP 2.3): big blocks in running bond, bevelled (lit top and left, dark bottom and right) with a joint along the bottom and right, each block its own tone, worn patches from noise.
  - Exports: `STONE`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators.test.ts)
- [`tiles.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/tiles.ts): The tile generator (`texture:tiles`, PLAN.md WP 13.17): glazed square tiles for a kitchen's or a bathroom's floor and walls: a tone per tile, a highlight along each tile's top row where the glaze catches the light, and sunk grout along its bottom and left; with `checker` tones, every other tile is of those, as a kitchen floor's checker.
  - Exports: `TILES`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts)
- [`wallpaper.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/wallpaper.ts): The wallpaper generator (`texture:wallpaper`, PLAN.md WP 13.17): a printed paper in vertical stripes, a narrow stripe at the left of each repeat and a small diamond in the middle of the wide band between, printed a little proud.
  - Exports: `WALLPAPER`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts)
- [`water.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/water.ts): The water generator (`texture:water`, PLAN.md WP 7.3): still water in two blue tones in broad patches, with ripple lines running across it (along x), bent by a slow swell and dithered on every other texel, as the 2D games paint a pond.
  - Exports: `WATER`, `wave`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v2.test.ts)
- [`wood.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/wood.ts): The wood generator (`texture:wood`, PLAN.md WP 13.17): plain wood for doors, furniture and trim, its grain running up (v): dark grain lines a few texels apart, wavering as a sawn board's do, over slow bands of its tones, and now and then a knot, a dark core in a ring that bends the grain round it.
  - Exports: `WOOD`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/v3.test.ts)

## engine/gfx/viewmodel

- [`material.ts`](../engine/gfx/viewmodel/material.ts): The viewmodel's materials (PLAN.md WP 13.12): first person's player is drawn by two meshes in the materials the stage gives them (engine/gfx/viewmodel/body.ts: the body and the arms), each in a node material copy of its own: - the body's (`body(material)`), on its skinned mesh, folds to a point every vertex whose `viewmodel` attribute is 1, so the camera sees none of the body, and draws its shadow from every vertex where skinning puts it (`castShadowPositionNode`), so the shadow stays whole; - the arms' (`arms(material)`), on a mesh the CPU poses, draws each vertex by the arms' lens (engine/gfx/viewmodel/ lens.ts: on its ray from the eye, at their own depth, spread by their own field of view) and takes the shadows falling where it really is (`receivedShadowPositionNode`), not where it is drawn, inside the body's own head.
  - Exports: `createViewmodelLook`, `VIEWMODEL_MATERIAL_CODES`, `ViewmodelLook`
  - Tests: [`engine/gfx/viewmodel/material.test.ts`](../engine/gfx/viewmodel/material.test.ts), [`tests/e2e/playground-cameras.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/playground-cameras.spec.ts)

- [`mantle.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/mantle.ts): The shooter model's mantle and superglide (PLAN.md WP 13.6, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2), as the Apex Movement Wiki measures them: up a ledge engine/physics/ledge.ts found, along its path, the feet moved straight along it (engine/physics/character.ts's `stepCharacter`: the path is clear, so no controller), in two timed phases.

  - Tests: [`engine/physics/movement/profile.test.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/profile.test.ts)
- [`profiles.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/profiles.ts): The movement profiles every game gets (PLAN.md WP 13.3, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2), registered on the shared registry when this module loads (engine/physics/character.ts loads it): - `movement:apex`, Apex Legends' movement: its medium legends' hull, steps and slopes, gravity, jump and grace period, and the shooter model at its defaults, which are Apex's numbers (engine/physics/movement/model.ts).
  - Exports: `MOVEMENT_PROFILES`
  - Tests: [`engine/physics/movement/profile.test.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/profile.test.ts)
- [`ride.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/ride.ts): The shooter model's rides (PLAN.md WP 13.7, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2): ziplines, the redeploy balloon's skydive and ladders, and launchers for every character.

  - Exports: `MOVEMENT_SETTINGS`, `MovementOverride`, `movementOverrides`, `tuneCharacter`
  - Tests: [`engine/physics/movement/settings.test.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/settings.test.ts)
- [`steer.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/steer.ts): One tick of the shooter model (PLAN.md WP 13.3, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2), in the order of Apex's own tick (er-apex's `controller.rs` `tick`, lines 551-700; MIT, engine/physics/movement/NOTICE): the timers and the climb space; a mantle's tick (engine/physics/movement/mantle.ts: the feet moved along its path, no controller), the superglide's crouch, a climb's tick (climb.ts); the duck and the slide it starts (crouch.ts), the sprint, a mantle or a climb starting (a jump at a ledge mantles instead), the jump, then the walk on the ground (engine/physics/movement/ground.ts; a slide's between the halves of its pull along the floor) or the lurch and the air move in the air (air.ts), then gravity, integrated exactly; after the controller's move, `settleMotion` takes a slide's step-up cost, lands (the fall stun, by the impact speed along the floor's normal; ducked, a landing slides), keeps the floor, the flight's count and turns the character toward where it faces at the model's turn rate (toward the wall while it mantles or climbs).
  - Exports: `Room`, `settleMotion`, `steerMotion`, `turnToward`
  - Tests: [`engine/physics/movement/steer.test.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/steer.test.ts)
