- [`glyph.ts`](../engine/world/level/glyph.ts): The legend registry (PLAN.md WP 2.2, WP 13.13, §6.6, I-22): the registry kind `glyph`, one entry per character a level map may hold, saying what that character means: its floor and top heights and how its floor runs (flat, a ramp, a dais, a flight of stairs to the storey above), whether it is solid, its collider and mesh recipes, nav flags, a spawn point, a light spot, a surface tag, whether a ladder stands on it and its footprint; and for levels written as storeys (format 2), void, full height, an opening (a door or a window), a head and a room marker (`STOREY_FIELDS`, which a format-1 level's legend leaves out).
  - Exports: `defineGlyph`, `Glyph`, `GLYPH_FIELDS`, `glyphKind`, `GlyphSpec`, `legendOf`, `STOREY_FIELDS`
  - Tests: [`engine/world/level/glyph.test.ts`](../engine/world/level/glyph.test.ts)
- [`grid.ts`](../engine/world/level/grid.ts): A level's tile grid (PLAN.md WP 2.2): its size, its tile size and the glyph of each tile, as compile.ts hands it to the descriptor builders (colliders.ts, meshes.ts), with the two questions both ask: which glyphs it holds, in id order, and whether a tile holds one of some glyphs.
  - Exports: `byText`, `glyphsOf`, `holds`, `TileGrid`
  - Tests: [`engine/world/level/compile.test.ts`](../engine/world/level/compile.test.ts)
- [`heights.ts`](../engine/world/level/heights.ts): Height, solid and surface queries on a compiled level (PLAN.md WP 2.2, WP 4.2, WP 13.13, §5.1): `floorHeight(level, x, z)`, the walkable surface's height at a point (the prototype's `floorH`: where feet, spawns and nav stand), `topHeight`, the top of whatever stands there (`topH`: a wall's top over its tiles, for shots and particles), `surfaceAt`, the surface tag underfoot (footsteps, particles), `solidAt` and `tileAt`; and in 3D, for levels written as storeys, `floorBelow(level, x, y, z)` and `surfaceBelow`, the highest surface at or under a point (a storey's floor, a solid's top, a roof, the ground), `storeyAt(level, y)` by height alone, `storeyBelow` by that surface, and `roomAt`.
  - Exports: `floorBelow`, `floorHeight`, `HeightSource`, `roomAt`, `solidAt`, `storeyAt`, `storeyBelow`, `surfaceAt`, `surfaceBelow`, `tileAt`, `topHeight`
  - Tests: [`engine/world/level/compile.test.ts`](../engine/world/level/compile.test.ts)
- [`legend.ts`](../engine/world/level/legend.ts): The engine's legend (PLAN.md WP 2.2, WP 4.2, I-22): the glyphs every level can use without defining any, as plain specs of the kind `glyph` (engine/world/level/glyph.ts declares the kind and registers these with it).
  - Exports: `V1_GLYPHS`, `V2_GLYPHS`, `V3_GLYPHS`, `V4_GLYPHS`
  - Tests: [`engine/world/level/glyph.test.ts`](../engine/world/level/glyph.test.ts)
- [`level.ts`](../engine/world/level/level.ts): Levels as registry entries (PLAN.md WP 2.2, §6.6, §6.9): the registry kind `level`, so a scene names its level by id (`defineScene('box:room', { level: 'level:room', … })`, engine/sim/scene.ts) and `x describe level` lists them.
  - Exports: `defineLevel`, `getLevel`, `LEVEL_FIELDS`, `LevelEntry`
  - Tests: [`engine/world/level/level.test.ts`](../engine/world/level/level.test.ts)
- [`meshes.ts`](../engine/world/level/meshes.ts): Mesh descriptors from a level's tiles (PLAN.md WP 2.2, §6.1 "data descriptors"): plain data saying which pieces the level meshes (WP 2.4, engine/gfx/level/) draw, with no three.js here.
  - Exports: `levelMeshes`
  - Tests: [`engine/world/level/compile.test.ts`](../engine/world/level/compile.test.ts)
- [`openings.ts`](../engine/world/level/openings.ts): Doors and windows (PLAN.md WP 13.13; docs/PLAYGROUND.md §6.1, §7.1): the openings in a storey's walls, found in its tiles.
  - Exports: `findOpenings`, `OpeningProblem`, `sidesOf`
  - Tests: [`engine/world/level/openings.test.ts`](../engine/world/level/openings.test.ts)
- [`parse.ts`](../engine/world/level/parse.ts): The level text format, read (PLAN.md WP 2.2, WP 13.13, §9.0; doctrine: Agent-accessible assets): optional front matter, then the map, one character per tile, or a map per storey.

- [`problems.ts`](../engine/world/level/problems.ts): What can be wrong with a level, and how it is said (PLAN.md WP 2.2, §6.8; doctrine: Agent-operable): the level codes, each naming its fix in the level's own terms, and `LevelProblem`, one problem at a line and column of the level's text.

- [`roofs.ts`](../engine/world/level/roofs.ts): Roofs (PLAN.md WP 13.13; docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.1, §6.1): the roof a storey's block gives (`roof: gable`, `hip` or `flat`), over the bounds of the storey's floored tiles and `eaves` past them.

## labs/anim/scenes

- [`lineup.ts`](../labs/anim/scenes/lineup.ts): The Animation Lab's scene, `lab:lineup` (PLAN.md WP 10.8; my-3d2dge's animlab, `src/starter/60-animlab.js`: its lineup, its timeline and its frozen key poses): the humanoid body on every build in a row, chibi to adult, and the mannequin when its build is registered (the clip library's rest body), all told the same thing from one clock, so the lineup stays in step: - `lab.anim.play`: a sample state, a pose or a stance as engine/anim/states.ts and poses.ts name them (`idle`, `cheer`, `ready`…), `walk` or `run` (each figure walks forward and is put back where it started), a move (`move:jab`…) swung again and again, a rest of `REST` s between swings, its blade's trail drawn while it strikes, or a clip of the library (`clip:cmu/Cartwheel`: retargeted to every build, looped; the page registers the sets); - `lab.anim.time`: timeline scrubbing, a move held that many seconds from its start (−1 plays), so its wind-up, strike and recovery can be stepped through frame by frame; `lab.anim.speed`: the rate a move plays at.
  - Exports: `LAB_FIGURE`, `lineup`, `LINEUP_AT`, `LINEUP_BUILDS`, `LINEUP_GAP`, `LINEUP_SETTINGS`, `LINEUP_STATES`, `REST`
  - Tests: [`labs/anim/scenes/lineup.test.ts`](../labs/anim/scenes/lineup.test.ts)

- [`air.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/air.ts): The air course, `course:playground-air` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.4): the player, empty-handed, placed at the west end of the open floor south of the slide ramps, sprints east holding sprint and jumps three times: 0.1 s into the first, a side key replaces forward (a lurch); the second it takes with a side key held from the take-off (an air strafe); the third it presses just before landing (a bunny hop); then it runs on and stops.
  - Exports: `AIR_START`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`bounds.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/bounds.ts): The bounds every playground course checks beside its own numbers (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §4, §5.1 and §9.1, PLAN.md WP 13.4): from the step after a course places the player, its body's (a planted foot slides at most 5 cm in one contact, the anim QA's limit; no point jumps past the QA's pop of 9/16 m in a step) and, for each of the playground's five cameras (labs/playground/views.ts), §4's: no frame moves the camera more than 0.3 m or turns it more than 4° beyond what the player's own move, the look and a blend account for (engine/dev/feel/camera.ts), none stands it inside the level, and none loses the player (first person: its arms); and no frame lets a wall cover first person's arms or its near plane cut them (WP 13.12, `clip`); with a gun, §5.1's muzzle within 2° of the aim while the sights are up (`muzzleBound`, WP 13.20).
  - Exports: `bodyBounds`, `BOUNDS`, `BoundsSpan`, `cameraBounds`, `muzzleBound`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`camera-walls.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/camera-walls.ts): The cameras' hard places, `course:playground-camera-walls` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §4, PLAN.md WP 13.8, its review): where a follow camera meets the level, the shooter's and the platformer's cameras held to §4's four bounds in four legs.
  - Exports: `CAMERA_WALLS`, `PITCH`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`cameras.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/cameras.ts): The cameras' soak course, `course:playground-cameras` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §4 and §9.1, PLAN.md WP 13.8): the player runs a square of about 10 m on the gym's floor by its north end, twice round (`LOOP`), sprinting and sliding east, jumping south, sprinting west a metre off the fences and running north between the 1.5 and 2 m mantle walls, turning a quarter at each corner as a player turns the view, while the camera cycles through the five modes (labs/playground/views.ts), a switch every `SWITCH` steps, each blended as the page's T blends it (the course's `views`).
  - Exports: `CAMERAS_START`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`climb.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/climb.ts): The climb course, `course:playground-climb` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.6): the player, empty-handed, sprints at each of the gym's climb walls and jumps 2.6 m short of its face, holding forward.
  - Exports: `BOUNCE_RUNS`, `CLIMB_RUNS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`climbAgain.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/climbAgain.ts): The climb-again course, `course:playground-climb-again` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.18): the player, empty-handed, sprints at the gym's 6 m climb wall and jumps 2.6 m short of its face, holding forward, as the climb course's neutral bounce does; climbing, it lets go (pulling back two ticks), then pushes at the wall again as it falls.
  - Exports: `CLIMB_AGAIN_START`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`crawl.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/crawl.ts): The crawl course, `course:playground-crawl` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.5): the player, empty-handed, crouch-walks into the crawl tunnel (1.4 m clear, 8 m long), lets crouch go inside and goes on crouched under the roof, standing up and running once out; then slides under the bar (1.3 m up) from a sprint.
  - Exports: `CRAWL_STARTS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`crouch.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/crouch.ts): The crouch course, `course:playground-crouch` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.18): the player, empty-handed and standing on the open floor east of the slope tests, crouches and holds it, stands up, then spams crouch, pressing it for 0.3 s at a time with 0.15 s between.
  - Exports: `CROUCH_START`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`fences.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/fences.ts): The fences course, `course:playground-fences` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.6): the player, empty-handed, sprints at each of the gym's fences (half a metre thick) from 1.5 m short of its face, pressing and holding jump once within the ledge probe of it: Apex has no vault, so a fence is mantled over.
  - Exports: `FENCE_RUNS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`gaps.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/gaps.ts): The gaps course, `course:playground-gaps` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.3 and §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.18): the jump's reach on the gym's lane of gaps, its platforms 1.5 m up and 3 m long.
  - Exports: `GAP_RUNS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`hang.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/hang.ts): The hang course, `course:playground-hang` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.6): the mantle hang.
  - Exports: `HANG_STARTS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`hill.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/hill.ts): The hill course, `course:playground-hill` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.2 and §5.1, PLAN.md WP 10.5): the player, empty-handed, placed at the hill's foot (labs/playground/scenes/hill.ts), runs up its flank east for 3 s (to about 7 m up, over slopes of 10° to 29°), turns and sprints down it west, slides from a crouch at the steepest stretch, gaining speed down the slope, and runs out at its foot; then the body's and every camera's bounds (labs/playground/courses/bounds.ts), so the feet stay planted on the terrain's slopes as on the gym's floors.
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`jumps.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/jumps.ts): The jumps course, `course:playground-jumps` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.4): the player, empty-handed, placed in the open floor between the slide ramps and the slope tests, jumps from standing, jumps again as it lands (the press buffered just before), then once more after a rest, then walks and crouch-walks south; its numbers against §3.2's, then the bounds (labs/playground/courses/bounds.ts).
  - Exports: `JUMPS_START`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`ladder.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/ladder.ts): The ladder course, `course:playground-ladder` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.7): the tower's ladder, up its north face to its 6 m top.
  - Exports: `LADDER_STARTS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`landing.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/landing.ts): The landing course, `course:playground-landing` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.18): the player, empty-handed, is placed in the air over the gym's open south floor, running east, and falls 6, 14 and 25 m: under the 7.62 m a fall keeps its speed from, between it and the 20.32 m the stun is full from, and past that.
  - Exports: `LANDING_RUNS`, `landingOf`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`launcher.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/launcher.ts): The launcher course, `course:playground-launcher` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.3, PLAN.md WP 13.7): the gym's jump pad and trampoline (labs/playground/levels/gym.ts).
  - Exports: `LAUNCHER_STARTS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`mantle.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/mantle.ts): The mantle course, `course:playground-mantle` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.6): the player, empty-handed, runs at each of the gym's mantle walls from 1.5 m short of its face, pressing and holding jump once its hull is within the ledge probe's 0.61 m of it, on the ground: Apex's auto mantle.
  - Exports: `MANTLE_RUNS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`range.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/range.ts): The range course, `course:playground-range` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.1 and §7.2, PLAN.md WP 13.20): at the range's bench (labs/playground/scenes/site.ts `playground:site-range`), the player draws the pistol, raises its sights and looks about, left and right, up and down (each look glided to over 12 steps, as a mouse turns it), firing a round; then the rifle, its sights up again, a burst held at each look.
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`skydive.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/skydive.ts): The skydive course, `course:playground-skydive` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.7): the redeploy balloon.
  - Exports: `SKYDIVE_START`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`slideFlat.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/slideFlat.ts): The flat slide course, `course:playground-slide-flat` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.5): the player, empty-handed, sprints south down the open lane beside the sprint strip and slides four times: a boosted slide let go fast, two inside the boost's cooldown, and a boosted one held to its end; its numbers against §3.2's, then the bounds (labs/playground/courses/bounds.ts).
  - Exports: `SLIDE_FLAT_START`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`slideJump.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/slideJump.ts): The slide-jump course, `course:playground-slide-jump` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.5): the player, empty-handed, sprints south down the open lane, slides, and jumps out of the slide three times: once its crouch is down, once while it is still going down (a dead slide), and once as the slide slows through the long jump's band; each run's numbers against §3.2's, then each run's bounds (labs/playground/courses/bounds.ts).
  - Exports: `SLIDE_JUMPS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`slideRamps.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/slideRamps.ts): The slide ramps course, `course:playground-slide-ramps` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.5): the player, empty-handed, is put on the deck of each slide ramp (5°, 10°, 20° and 30°, 12 m long) at a holstered sprint's 7.59 m/s, crouching, so it slides off the deck, down the ramp and out across the run-out; then at the 30° ramp's foot, sliding up it.
  - Exports: `SLIDE_RAMPS`, `SLIDE_UPHILL`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`steps.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/steps.ts): The steps-and-slopes course, `course:playground-steps` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.3 and §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.18): the player, empty-handed, runs south up the gym's stairs (four 0.25 m risers, each step 1 m deep, to 1 m), up the slope test at 45°, just inside the walkable limit of 45.57°, to its deck 4 m up, and at the one at 51°, past it, which it never stands on.
  - Exports: `STEP_RUNS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`strip.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/strip.ts): The strip course, `course:playground-strip` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.3 and §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.4): the player, empty-handed (holstered: every speed ×1.15), placed at the strip's north end, runs south from standing for 1.5 s, sprints on a press (the sticky sprint keeps it), then lets go and stops; its numbers against §3.2's, then the bounds (labs/playground/courses/bounds.ts).
  - Exports: `STRIP_START`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`superglide.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/superglide.ts): The superglide courses (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.6): `course:playground-superglide` sprints at the 1.5 m mantle wall holding jump (the auto mantle: the grab, 27 ticks, then the pull, 18) and, in the pull's last 0.15 s (its last 9 ticks), lets jump go and presses it, then presses crouch the very next tick: the superglide, about 13.7 m/s out of the mantle (Apex's 540 u/s; ours 1.8 × the holstered sprint, 13.67).
  - Exports: `GLIDE_START`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)
- [`zipline.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/zipline.ts): The zipline course, `course:playground-zipline` (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2, PLAN.md WP 13.7): the tower's 40 m zipline and the balloon's line.
  - Exports: `ZIPLINE_STARTS`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts`](../labs/playground/courses/courses.test.ts)

  - Exports: `HOUSE_MAP`, `HOUSE_MARKERS`, `HOUSE_RECTS`, `HOUSE_ROOMS`, `HOUSE_TEXT`, `HOUSE_TILE`

- [`plan.ts`](../labs/playground/levels/plan.ts): Storey plans (PLAN.md WP 13.18): how the playground writes its buildings as storeys (level format 2, engine/world/level/parse.ts) from rectangles in metres, not character by character.
  - Exports: `levelText`, `Plan`, `Rect`, `StoreyBlock`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/levels/house.test.ts`](../labs/playground/levels/house.test.ts)
- [`site.ts`](../labs/playground/levels/site.ts): The block (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2, PLAN.md WP 13.18): the playground's one site, `site:block`, 96 × 113 m of terrain (`terrain:site`: the hill's ground, labs/playground/scenes/hill.ts, flattened under the yards, the range and the street) and the structures standing on it, in world metres (+X east, +Z south): - the range along the north edge (z 0 to 12, x 0 to 60): its shelter at x 2 to 6, its backstop at x 58; the ring east of it (x 60 to 72); - the gym as built (WP 13.1 to 13.7), 41 × 101 m from (0, 12), its wall open by three gates (`GYM_GATES`): the §2 sketch's 36 × 70 m strip could not hold it, so the block runs 17 m further south than §2's 96 m (amendment 20); - the backyard (x 41 to 72, z 12 to 44): the tree house, the shed; the house (labs/playground/levels/house.ts) with its garage, patio and porch at (44, 44); the front yard (z 63 to 83) with its path and the driveway; - the street (z 83 to 95, x 41 to 96), from the gym's east gate to the block's east edge; the hill (x 72 to 96), rising to 10 m over the east edge's middle, the lookout on its top.
  - Exports: `SITE`, `SITE_AREAS`, `SITE_SIZE`, `SITE_STRUCTURES`, `SiteArea`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/scenes/site.test.ts`](../labs/playground/scenes/site.test.ts)
- [`street.ts`](../labs/playground/levels/street.ts): The site's paving (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.2, PLAN.md WP 13.18): levels of one storey on 0.5 m tiles that labs/playground/levels/site.ts lays on the block, each drawn in its own surface (their entries' recipes): - **The street** (`level:street`): 55 × 12 m, a road 8 m wide in asphalt, its dashed middle line in paint, between two sidewalks 2 m wide in concrete, 0.15 m up (`,`, the playground's sidewalk glyph: the curb a step).
  - Exports: `CURB`, `DRIVEWAY_TEXT`, `PATH_TEXT`, `PAVING_TILE`, `STREET`, `STREET_TEXT`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/scenes/site.test.ts`](../labs/playground/scenes/site.test.ts)
- [`yard.ts`](../labs/playground/levels/yard.ts): The site's small buildings (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.2, PLAN.md WP 13.18), each a level written as storeys on 0.5 m tiles (labs/playground/levels/plan.ts), which labs/playground/levels/site.ts stands on the block: - **The shed** (`level:shed`): 3 × 4 m and 2.5 m high under a flat roof bodies stand on, a door and a window.
  - Exports: `BACKSTOP_TEXT`, `DECK_HEIGHT`, `LOOKOUT_TEXT`, `RING_TEXT`, `SHED_TEXT`, `SHELTER_TEXT`, `TREEHOUSE_TEXT`, `YARD_TILE`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/scenes/site.test.ts`](../labs/playground/scenes/site.test.ts)

## labs/playground/looks

- [`cel.ts`](../labs/playground/looks/cel.ts): The look `look:playground-cel`, the playground cel-shaded (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.2, PLAN.md WP 13.24): the toon style's ramp per material (three bands of light and a rim, each material's shadows its own colour shifted in hue, cooler and more saturated, rather than darkened: `shade`), ink from depth and normals at sharp creases, the outline shells round the props and the bodies (skinned ones too, engine/gfx/stageShells.ts), both 1 px at 270 lines and scaled to the picture's lines in whole pixels, and the sky's dome as a clean gradient (`skyGradient`).
  - Exports: `look`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/looks/looks.test.ts`](../labs/playground/looks/looks.test.ts), [`tests/e2e/playground-looks.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/playground-looks.spec.ts)
- [`pixel.ts`](../labs/playground/looks/pixel.ts): The look `look:playground-pixel`, the playground as pixel art (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.2, PLAN.md WP 13.24): a low-resolution picture at a whole-number scale (the pixel filter's `size` 0: the largest whole block giving 240 to 360 lines, one drawn pixel in the engine's `pixels` resolution, engine/gfx/post/grid.ts), 1-pixel ink from depth and normals, each material a ramp of four shades its shadows shifted in hue, its steps mixed by an ordered dither fixed to the world (the toon style's `dither`, its cells counted from the snap), 24 shades a channel.
  - Exports: `look`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/looks/looks.test.ts`](../labs/playground/looks/looks.test.ts), [`tests/e2e/playground-looks.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/playground-looks.spec.ts)
- [`pixelPerspective.ts`](../labs/playground/looks/pixelPerspective.ts): The look `look:playground-pixel-perspective`, the pixel look's variant for the perspective cameras (first person, the shooter and the platformer; docs/PLAYGROUND.md §5.2, PLAN.md WP 13.24): the chain draws its filters and toon numbers in place of `look:playground-pixel`'s while the camera is a perspective one (the look's `perspective`, engine/gfx/post/chain.ts), its style and sky staying the pixel look's.
  - Exports: `look`, `PIXEL_FILTERS`, `PIXEL_TOON`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/looks/looks.test.ts`](../labs/playground/looks/looks.test.ts)

## labs/playground/ui

- [`frontEnd.ts`](../labs/playground/ui/frontEnd.ts): The playground's front end (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §8.3, PLAN.md WP 13.25): its screens over the game, the engine's menus (engine/ui/menu.ts) and the playground's panels, on a stack (closing one shows the one under it again): - the title screen (`title`: Play, Spawn, Settings, Photo mode), shown as the page opens while the view setting `playground.title` says so (`auto`: unless a replay plays or automation drives the browser, as the menu for humans; `on`, `off`); Escape plays; - pause (`pause`: Resume, Spawn, Settings, Photo mode, Restart, Title screen), opened by the system layer's `pause` (Escape, the pad's Start) or by the pointer lock let go while the map wants it (a browser spends the first Escape on the lock); - the spawn picker (`spawns`, labs/playground/ui/spawns.ts), settings (`settings`, labs/playground/ui/settings.ts) and photo mode (`photo`, labs/playground/ui/photo.ts).
  - Exports: `createFrontEnd`, `FRONT_END_SETTINGS`, `FrontEnd`, `FrontEndOptions`, `ScreenName`, `spawnOnOpen`, `titleOnOpen`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/playground.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/playground.spec.ts)
- [`hud.ts`](../labs/playground/ui/hud.ts): The playground's HUD by camera mode (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §8.3, PLAN.md WP 13.25): what each of the five modes shows over the game (`HUD_MODES`), and `showHud`, which the page (labs/playground/main.ts) runs each drawn frame: - the camera and the look in use, top right, and the room the player is in on a scene's site, top left; - the crosshair where the screen's centre aims a gun (first person and the shooter: `showsCrosshair`, labs/playground/weapons/hud.ts), never in the views that aim with the pointer; - the prompts: what using the thing in reach does, with the key that uses it on the device used last (WP 13.16); - the ammo: the weapon out and its rounds, the range's count (`weaponLine`, WP 13.20); - the keys of the map in use, as its prompts give them (`keysLine`, labs/playground/controls.ts); - the feel readout (`feelLine`): the player's speed over the ground and how he moves (the movement model's mode or gait), which the platformer, isometric and top-down show (where the view gives speed away least), and every mode with the view setting `playground.readout` at `on` (`off` hides it everywhere).
  - Exports: `feelLine`, `HUD_MODES`, `HUD_SETTINGS`, `HudFrame`, `HudMode`, `HudPlayer`, `showHud`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/ui/hud.test.ts`](../labs/playground/ui/hud.test.ts)
- [`photo.ts`](../labs/playground/ui/photo.ts): The playground's photo mode (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §8.3, PLAN.md WP 13.25): the run paused, the free camera (the engine's fly camera, a bare `cam3=fly`, which starts from the camera on screen: engine/gfx/cameras/fly.ts) flown with the map's move keys, the jump key climbing and the crouch key sinking, the sprint key fast; turned by dragging the mouse over the game (`PHOTO.drag` rad a pixel); its lens narrowed and widened with the wheel, as ever; the HUD hidden; the looks switched with P, as ever.
  - Exports: `createPhoto`, `Photo`, `PHOTO`, `PhotoCamera`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/playground.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/playground.spec.ts)
- [`prefs.ts`](../labs/playground/ui/prefs.ts): The playground's preferences (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §8.3, PLAN.md WP 13.25): what its settings screen changes and the page's store keeps across sessions (`createStore`, engine/app/store.ts, under `PREFS_PREFIX`): the camera mode the page opens in, the settings of `PREF_SETTINGS` by path (the field of view, the mouse, the look, the quality, the movement profile) and the audio buses' levels.
  - Exports: `NO_PREFS`, `PREF_BUSES`, `PREF_SETTINGS`, `Prefs`, `PREFS_KEY`, `PREFS_PREFIX`, `PrefSetting`, `prefsQuery`, `readPrefs`, `savePrefs`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/ui/prefs.test.ts`](../labs/playground/ui/prefs.test.ts)
- [`settings.ts`](../labs/playground/ui/settings.ts): The playground's settings screen (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §8.3, PLAN.md WP 13.25): a panel over the game, in the look of the engine's menus (engine/ui/widgets.ts's box), with a row for each thing the player sets (`SETTING_ROWS`): the camera mode, the field of view, the mouse's sensitivity and its inversion, the movement profile, the look, the quality and whether the frame rate may move it (the governor, engine/dev/governor.ts), and the four audio levels; then the controls: each action the player answers with its key, a button to rebind it, and one to reset them all.
  - Exports: `CONTROL_ACTIONS`, `createSettings`, `RowSchema`, `SETTING_ROWS`, `SettingRow`, `SettingsOptions`, `SettingsScreen`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/playground.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/playground.spec.ts)
- [`spawns.ts`](../labs/playground/ui/spawns.ts): The spawn picker's places (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §8.3, PLAN.md WP 13.25): each area of the block (`SITE_AREAS`: its spawn, facing as it faces) and each room of its structures (`roomPlace`, labs/playground/scenes/site.ts: at the room's marker, ducked under a low ceiling), each as the arguments of the block's dev action `place`, so a pick is a recorded operation of the run and its replay holds it.
  - Exports: `SPAWN_SETTINGS`, `spawnPlace`, `SpawnPlace`, `spawnPlaces`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/ui/spawns.test.ts`](../labs/playground/ui/spawns.test.ts)

## labs/playground/weapons

- [`guns.ts`](../labs/playground/weapons/guns.ts): The playground's firearms (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §7.2, PLAN.md WP 13.20): a pistol and a rifle, each a prop built from parts (`prop:playground-pistol`, `prop:playground-rifle`: boxes and a barrel, in the weapon's frame, the grip at the origin and +Z along the barrel, no body) and a weapon of the kind `weapon` (engine/world/weapons.ts) with Apex Legends' season 3 numbers for its rate, damage, magazine and reloads; its cones, recoil, sights and draw are ours, shaped like the game's (a pistol's single kick, a rifle's climb that drifts right, then left): - **The pistol** (`weapon:playground-pistol`, the P2020's): semi-automatic at 7 shots a second, 18 points a shot, 10 rounds, a 1.25 s reload either way, a tight cone from the hip, a little kick a shot, quick to draw; - **The rifle** (`weapon:playground-rifle`, the R-301's): automatic at 13.5 shots a second, 14 points a shot, 18 rounds, 2.4 s to reload, 3.2 s from empty, a wider cone from the hip, a burst climbing up and to the right, then left, its sights 55° at Apex's 70° lens (WP 13.8's rifles').
  - Exports: `GUN_PROPS`, `PISTOL`, `PLAYGROUND_WEAPONS`, `RIFLE`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/weapons/range.test.ts`](../labs/playground/weapons/range.test.ts)
- [`hud.ts`](../labs/playground/weapons/hud.ts): The firearms' HUD line (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §7.2, PLAN.md WP 13.20): what the page (labs/playground/main.ts) shows of the player's weapons (engine/sim/weapons.ts's component `weapons`) each frame: the weapon out and its rounds, or that it reloads, or holstered; and the range's count, his hits and his accuracy, the share of his shots that struck a standing target or a person (`weaponLine`).
  - Exports: `showsCrosshair`, `weaponLine`, `WeaponsView`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/weapons/range.test.ts`](../labs/playground/weapons/range.test.ts)
- [`range.ts`](../labs/playground/weapons/range.ts): The range's targets (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.2, §7.2; PLAN.md WP 13.20): things (WP 10.4, engine/world/things.ts) standing as `prop:playground-target` down its three lanes (z 3, 6 and 9), facing the bench at x 4 (`RANGE_TARGETS`): pop-up targets at 10 and 25 m (`thing:playground-popper`), and at 50 m moving ones sliding across their lane (`thing:playground-mover`, 2 m to and fro at 1 m/s).
  - Exports: `FALL`, `MOVER`, `POPPER`, `Popup`, `POPUP_FIELDS`, `RANGE_TARGETS`, `standRange`, `standTarget`
  - Tests: [`labs/playground/weapons/range.test.ts`](../labs/playground/weapons/range.test.ts)

- [`puppets.ts`](../tests/pages/puppets.ts): The puppets page's module (tests/pages/puppets.html, PLAN.md WP 3.8): the engine's renderer with a lit scene (a hemisphere light and one shadow-casting sun: one shadow map) and four things to show, one at a time, each registered with the warm-up before the first frame: - the neutral humanoid (`body:humanoid`, build:chibi) as one rigid-skinned puppet (engine/gfx/puppets/draw.ts), in the page's test pose (`testPose`: every joint turned up to 0.5 rad about a seeded axis, the root turned 0.6 rad); - the socket marks (fixtures/bodies/socketMarks.ts) in the same build and pose, as a puppet of their own; - a crowd of instanced humanoids (`createPuppetBatches`) with blob shadows, on a grid 1.5 m apart, each in a seeded pose of its own; - the fixture body `body:everyPart` (fixtures/bodies/everyPart.ts), one part of every type, in the same build: one rigid-skinned puppet and two instanced ones of its own batches (`parts/…`), one facing the camera and one turned away (its cape), so every part type is drawn both ways.
  - Exports: `CrowdShown`, `EveryPartShown`, `HumanoidShown`, `MARK_SHOT`, `SocketShot`, `testPose`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/puppets.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/puppets.spec.ts)
- [`replay.ts`](../tests/pages/replay.ts): The replay page's module (`tests/pages/replay.html`), Chromium's half of `node x replay --browser sim` (PLAN.md §6.5 item 9, WP 1.5): the sim in a page with no renderer.
- [`scene.ts`](../tests/pages/scene.ts): The scene page's module (tests/pages/scene.html): the fixture scene (tests/pages/sceneFixture.ts) drawn by the engine's renderer (engine/gfx/renderer.ts) for the render tests, which drive it through `window.__scene` and import the modules they test into the page (`await import('/engine/gfx/pipelines.ts')`): the same module instances the page runs.
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/renderer.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/renderer.spec.ts)
- [`sceneFixture.ts`](../tests/pages/sceneFixture.ts): The scene page's fixture (tests/pages/scene.html): a small scene as plain data, and `buildScene`, which turns a description into three.js objects.
  - Exports: `buildScene`, `BuiltScene`, `FIXTURE`, `LightSpec`, `MaterialSpec`, `MeshSpec`, `PoolSpec`, `SceneDescription`, `ShapeSpec`
- [`shading.ts`](../tests/pages/shading.ts): The shading page's module (tests/pages/shading.html, PLAN.md WP 11.5): a small lit corner drawn through the post chain (engine/gfx/post/chain.ts), for what its shading sections do where the box has nothing to show them on: a steel ball and a steel plate on the floor (metalness 1: the box draws no metal; its iron is on props it never places), before a red wall and a blue one meeting in a corner with a white block in it, a sun that casts, two pillars cutting its light, and a lamp.
  - Exports: `ScreenBox`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/enhanced.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/enhanced.spec.ts)
- [`shot.ts`](../tests/pages/shot.ts): The shot page's module (tests/pages/shot.html): a fixture scene made for the ID pass and the look metrics, drawn by the engine's renderer (engine/gfx/renderer.ts), and `window.__engine` with `ready`, `errors`, `info()` and `shot(options)`: engine/gfx/shot.ts's `shot`, returned as JSON through `shotForJson`, the member `x shot` calls (WP 2.7 registers the engine's own, §8.3).
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/shot.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/shot.spec.ts)
- [`ui.ts`](../tests/pages/ui.ts): The UI widgets page's module (tests/pages/ui.html), the browser half of tests/e2e/ui.spec.ts (PLAN.md WP 10.6): the overlay (engine/ui/overlay.ts) over the page's canvas with a health bar and hearts in the top-left place, a quest box in the top-right one, a dialog, a pause menu and a settings panel (`#panel`) the gamepad's cursor works (engine/ui/{widgets,dialog,menu}.ts), all reading the page's real input (engine/input/input.ts) over its window, with gamepads through a stubbed `navigator.getGamepads` whose slots the tests fill with scripted pads.

## tools/anim

- [`asf-amc-fixture.ts`](../tools/anim/asf-amc-fixture.ts): A CMU-like skeleton and takes written here as text for the CMU tools' tests (WP 8.5; no capture is committed): `testAsf()`, the database's 30 bones with made-up proportions, and `testAmc(n)`, a take of `n` frames at 120 a second in which the subject walks forward (its legs and arms swing, once a second) or, with `travel` 0, steps in place.
  - Exports: `testAmc`, `testAsf`
  - Tests: [`tools/anim/asf-amc.test.ts`](../tools/anim/asf-amc.test.ts)
- [`asf-amc.ts`](../tools/anim/asf-amc.ts): The Acclaim skeleton and motion formats the CMU motion capture database uses (PLAN.md §5.3, WP 8.5): `.asf`, a subject's bones, and `.amc`, a take, the bones' angles frame by frame, and the forward kinematics that pose a skeleton from a frame.
  - Exports: `AmcFrame`, `AsfBone`, `mm`, `mv`, `pose`, `readAmc`, `readAsf`, `Skeleton`, `tr`, `V`
  - Tests: [`tools/anim/asf-amc.test.ts`](../tools/anim/asf-amc.test.ts)
- [`cmu-capture.ts`](../tools/anim/cmu-capture.ts): CMU takes turned into captures (PLAN.md §5.3, WP 8.5): `readCmu` cuts picked stretches of a subject's takes (tools/anim/asf-amc.ts reads and poses them) into the captures the importer fits (engine/anim/clip/encode.ts `Capture`: the 36 body points in the rig's frame, f forward, r right, z up, centred on the root on the ground), like any other library's.
  - Exports: `CmuCapture`, `CmuOptions`, `Pick`, `readCmu`
  - Tests: [`tools/anim/asf-amc.test.ts`](../tools/anim/asf-amc.test.ts)
- [`cmu-cli.ts`](../tools/anim/cmu-cli.ts): `x anim cmu …` (PLAN.md §5.3, WP 8.5): the CMU database's subcommands, ported from `my-3d2dge:tools/cmu.mjs` (`find`, `subject`, `get`, `all`, `survey`, `library`, `ledger`) with the ledger split and every take fetched into `.cache/anim/cmu/` by HTTP ranges (tools/anim/cmu.ts), plus `rates`, which verifies the frame rate of takes the site's list leaves out (tools/anim/rates.ts).
  - Exports: `CMU_SUBCOMMANDS`, `CmuRequest`, `cmuTargets`, `runCmu`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/anim.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/anim.test.ts)
- [`cmu.ts`](../tools/anim/cmu.ts): The CMU Graphics Lab Motion Capture Database (mocap.cs.cmu.edu), fetched on demand into `.cache/anim/` (PLAN.md §5.3 and §10.3, WP 8.5): about 2,500 takes by 113 subjects, each subject a skeleton (`NN.asf`) and each take a motion (`NN_MM.amc`) at 120 frames a second (some at 60).
  - Exports: `ANIM_CACHE`, `ARCHIVE`, `asfOf`, `CMU_CACHE`, `cmuAll`, `cmuArchive`, `cmuGet`, `cmuIndex`, `IndexedTake`, `parseMotionList`, `SITE`
  - Tests: [`tools/anim/cmu.test.ts`](../tools/anim/cmu.test.ts)
- [`contacts.ts`](../tools/anim/contacts.ts): Contacts and events, detected at import (PLAN.md §10.2, WP 8.8; ADR-0010 amendment 7): when each foot and hand holds the ground or a surface (a clip's `contacts`), and the moments gameplay listens for (its `events`: `step`, `land`, `hit`), read from a capture's 36 body points.
  - Exports: `AIRBORNE`, `CARRY`, `detectContacts`, `FOOT_CLEAR`, `HAND_FLOOR`, `HANG`, `HOLD`, `HOLD_REACH`, `STILL`, `treadmill`
  - Tests: [`tools/anim/contacts.test.ts`](../tools/anim/contacts.test.ts)
- [`cut.ts`](../tools/anim/cut.ts): A smaller set cut from bigger ones (PLAN.md §5.3, WP 8.5): the clips a game adopts, with the records of the libraries they came from (their rest bodies and origins) and the mannequin's look, read from and written as set directories, one file a clip (tools/anim/repack.ts).
  - Exports: `cutSet`
  - Tests: [`tools/anim/cut.test.ts`](../tools/anim/cut.test.ts)
- [`cycle.ts`](../tools/anim/cycle.ts): The loop-cycle search (PLAN.md §5.3, WP 8.5): the best cycle in a stretch of a take, a stride or a hop, the span whose end matches its start in pose and in speed.
  - Exports: `bestCycle`
  - Tests: [`tools/anim/asf-amc.test.ts`](../tools/anim/asf-amc.test.ts)
- [`fetch.ts`](../tools/anim/fetch.ts): The re-import's sources (PLAN.md §10, WP 8.8): where each set's originals come from, whether this repository can reach them, and the fetch of Mesh2Motion's three `.glb` files into `.cache/anim/mesh2motion/` (never committed), each at a pinned commit and checked against its sha256, through `curl` (tools/anim/zip.ts `fetchBytes`), which follows the environment's proxy.
  - Exports: `fetchMesh2Motion`, `MESH2MOTION`, `MESH2MOTION_CACHE`, `SET_SOURCES`, `SetSource`
  - Tests: [`tools/anim/upgrade.test.ts`](../tools/anim/upgrade.test.ts)
- [`find.ts`](../tools/anim/find.ts): Searching the library (PLAN.md §10.3, WP 8.5): `x anim find <words>` looks through every set's generated `catalog.tsv` (data/anim/sets/<set>/, tools/anim/repack.ts), then the CMU ledger's takes not yet in a set (tools/anim/ledger.ts), so an agent picks a clip without opening the library.

## tools/eslint

- [`askTheEntry.ts`](../tools/eslint/askTheEntry.ts): The local rule "ask the entry, never the id" (PLAN.md §6.6, ADR-0012): shared code reads an entry's hooks and fields, each with a default on the kind's schema, and never compares a registered id, so new content works without editing the code that uses it.
  - Exports: `default`, `ID_SHAPE`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/askTheEntry.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/askTheEntry.test.ts)
- [`banned.ts`](../tools/eslint/banned.ts): The banned and renamed three.js APIs (PLAN.md Appendix B; doctrine: Mastery), scoped by path, each message naming the replacement: legacy and fragile APIs, names from releases newer than the pinned r182, r182's deprecations (any deprecation warning fails a test anyway), and GPU readbacks outside the two files allowed them.
  - Exports: `BANNED_FILES`, `BANNED_IMPORT_FILES`, `bannedBlocks`, `bannedPlugin`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/banned.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/banned.test.ts)
- [`family.ts`](../tools/eslint/family.ts): Plumbing for the rule families of eslint.config.js: core rules re-exposed under a family's own name, and per-path zones for bans that have exceptions.
  - Exports: `Ban`, `family`, `messagesOf`, `resolvingImports`, `shortest`, `zoned`
- [`index.ts`](../tools/eslint/index.ts): The local ESLint plugin and the rule families eslint.config.js assembles (PLAN.md §6.1, §6.5, §6.10, Appendix B): one module per family, each exporting its blocks, and `local`, the plugin for what no stock rule expresses.
  - Exports: `askTheEntryBlocks`, `bannedBlocks`, `family`, `layerBlocks`, `local`, `publicApiBlocks`, `simSideBlocks`
- [`layers.ts`](../tools/eslint/layers.ts): The layer rules (PLAN.md §6.1; doctrines: WebGPU only, Reproducible): one `no-restricted-imports` block per engine layer, naming what the layer may import, so a forbidden edge fails T0 with the rule and the way round it.
  - Exports: `layerBlocks`, `layerPlugin`, `THREE_MATH`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/layers.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/layers.test.ts)
- [`namespaceNames.ts`](../tools/eslint/namespaceNames.ts): `banned/no-namespace-names` (PLAN.md Appendix B, WP 1.6): a banned three.js name read off a namespace of its entry point, however the namespace is named or the name is spelt.
  - Exports: `EntryName`, `namespaceNames`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/banned.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/banned.test.ts)
- [`publicApi.ts`](../tools/eslint/publicApi.ts): The public-API rule (PLAN.md §6.1, ADR-0020; doctrine: Quality under the hood): game code imports the engine only through its barrels, `engine/index.ts` (pages) and `engine/sim-api.ts` (sim-side code), and never three.js or Rapier directly, so game agents never depend on, or need to read, the internals.
  - Exports: `publicApiBlocks`, `publicApiPlugin`, `SIM_SIDE_GAME_CODE`, `unnamedImports`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/publicApi.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/publicApi.test.ts)
- [`simSide.ts`](../tools/eslint/simSide.ts): The reproducibility bans for sim-side code (PLAN.md §6.5, Appendix B; doctrine: Reproducible): no clocks, no unseeded randomness, no DOM, no Web Audio, no three.js, so identical inputs and seeds give identical play in Node and in Chromium.
  - Exports: `SIM_SIDE`, `simPlugin`, `simSideBlocks`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/simSide.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/simSide.test.ts)
- [`testing.ts`](../tools/eslint/testing.ts): Lints fixtures for the ESLint tests (WP 0.4): writes each source at its repository path inside a temporary directory and lints it through ESLint's Node API with eslint.config.js's own `configure(…)`, so every rule is proved by a failing and a passing fixture, and nothing failing is ever committed.
  - Exports: `ALL_ON`, `Case`, `caseProblems`, `CaseResult`, `ConfigModule`, `describeMessages`, `lintCases`, `lintFixtures`, `loadConfigModule`, `Switches`, `uncovered`
  - Tests: [`tools/eslint/config.test.ts`](../tools/eslint/config.test.ts)

## tools/mcp

- [`backend.ts`](../tools/mcp/backend.ts): What the MCP bridge's tools run on (PLAN.md §8.11, WP 7.6): a `Backend`, the engine as one interface, whichever process holds it.
  - Exports: `Backend`, `OpenArgs`, `Opened`, `openPath`, `Params`, `Progress`
  - Tests: [`tools/mcp/server.test.ts`](../tools/mcp/server.test.ts)
- [`docs.ts`](../tools/mcp/docs.ts): The MCP bridge's `docs_lookup` (PLAN.md §8.11, WP 7.6): the manual that `x docs` generates, for an agent that reads no files.
  - Exports: `docsLookup`
  - Tests: [`tools/mcp/tools.test.ts`](../tools/mcp/tools.test.ts)
- [`headless.ts`](../tools/mcp/headless.ts): The MCP bridge's headless backend (PLAN.md §8.11, WP 7.6): `createHeadless` in this process, with the scene's view (engine/app/headless.ts `view: true`, no GPU), so `scene.dump` and `camera` answer, and no renderer, so no shot (`renders: false`).
  - Exports: `headlessBackend`, `invoke`, `sceneTarget`
  - Tests: [`tools/mcp/server.test.ts`](../tools/mcp/server.test.ts)
- [`link.ts`](../tools/mcp/link.ts): How the MCP server reaches its backend worker (PLAN.md §8.11, WP 7.6): requests and replies over a `WorkerLink`.
  - Exports: `forkLink`, `localLink`, `WorkerHandler`, `WorkerLink`, `WorkerReply`, `WorkerRequest`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/mcp.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/mcp.test.ts), [`tools/mcp/link.test.ts`](../tools/mcp/link.test.ts)
- [`results.ts`](../tools/mcp/results.ts): What the MCP bridge's tools answer (PLAN.md §8.11, WP 7.6): MCP `CallToolResult`s made from what the members return.
  - Exports: `cutText`, `errorLine`, `errorResult`, `GoldenVerdict`, `judgeGoldens`, `MAX_LISTED`, `MAX_TEXT`, `shotResult`, `shotSummary`, `valueResult`
  - Tests: [`tools/mcp/tools.test.ts`](../tools/mcp/tools.test.ts)
- [`schema.ts`](../tools/mcp/schema.ts): The MCP bridge's input schemas (PLAN.md §8.11, WP 7.6): the schema language's fields (engine/core/schema.ts), which inspector members declare their arguments in (engine/dev/members.ts), projected onto JSON Schema, the form MCP's tool list carries.
  - Exports: `argsSchema`, `fieldSchema`, `JsonSchema`, `McpSchemaError`, `ObjectSchema`
  - Tests: [`tools/mcp/tools.test.ts`](../tools/mcp/tools.test.ts)
- [`server.ts`](../tools/mcp/server.ts): The MCP server `x mcp` runs (PLAN.md §8.11, WP 7.6), on the official SDK's `Server`: the low-level one, since its tools are generated at run time as JSON Schema from the inspector's member table, which the SDK's `McpServer` takes only as zod schemas (a dependency of ours, which the bridge does without).
  - Exports: `Bridge`, `BridgeOptions`, `createBridge`, `WATCHED`
  - Tests: [`tools/cmd/mcp.test.ts`](../tools/cmd/mcp.test.ts), [`tools/mcp/server.test.ts`](../tools/mcp/server.test.ts)
- [`session.ts`](../tools/mcp/session.ts): The MCP bridge's page backend (PLAN.md §8.11, WP 7.6): a page open in the `x inspect` session (tools/cmd/inspect.ts), on WebGPU in the platform's Chromium, the backend `x mcp` serves by default.
  - Exports: `memberExpression`, `pageBackend`, `PROGRESS_MS`
  - Tests: [`tests/e2e/mcp.spec.ts`](../tests/e2e/mcp.spec.ts), [`tools/mcp/session.test.ts`](../tools/mcp/session.test.ts)
- [`tools.ts`](../tools/mcp/tools.ts): The MCP bridge's tools (PLAN.md §8.11, WP 7.6): each calls an inspector member, and its input schema is that member's argument schema projected onto JSON Schema (tools/mcp/schema.ts), its description the member's help line, so `help()`, the inspector's argument checks and the tools come from one table (shardfall's tool table, PLAN.md §5.8).
  - Exports: `positional`, `replayFile`, `runTool`, `ToolContext`, `toolList`
  - Tests: [`tools/mcp/tools.test.ts`](../tools/mcp/tools.test.ts)

  - Tests: [`tools/mcp/server.test.ts`](../tools/mcp/server.test.ts)
